tier_board.surface: Polaris reading, measured as time-to-comprehension: the cost of getting the owner's sentence ("open one place, understand what a project's vision and goals are") answered from the fresh capture.
tier_board.movement_note: No prior run measured comprehension cost, so there is no tier to move. What the fresh capture shows against the two prior readings of this territory (S1 "solid" first reading, L2 "world-class" cold-open, owner aborted the walkthrough 2026-09-05 as "Polaris unusable") is that both prior verdicts and the owner's are all defensible at once, because they measured different distances into the same document. The first 639 body words of the fresh capture are a good manifesto (S1/L2 are right); the page as served is 10,173 visible body words and 26,630 with its 364 disclosures opened (the owner is right). Nothing on the page reconciles those two facts for a reader, which is exactly what this lens says is missing.

themes.title: The ceiling is beaten; the exponent is not.
themes.text: P0-CEILING is resolved [Observed]: 1,504,691 B against 2,097,152 (V1-F1). But lane A removed a fixed cost, not a per-item cost, so growth reverted to tracking Butlers: the 1.4 MB working-target shortfall grew 78,637 -> 104,691 B in nine days on population alone (V1-F3), per-item cost is flat at ~1,473 B (V1-F2), and nine days of machine growth landed in projectShape as existing rows got fatter, not as new rows (L11-F3 [Inferred]). Straight-line arrival is ~2027-04 for the page and ~2027-07 for the machine body [Inferred] (L11-F6); P-80 Q1's 'complete population always served' forecloses paging, so the honest levers are per-item bytes: 729 tuple spans at 425,354 chars (S4-F1), the four-attribute framing quad at 300,210 B (S8-F1, direction corrected by C1-F2), and on the machine side two per-row fields that restate their own block header, 740,796 B or 13.2% of the body (L11-F4).

themes.title: Computed, then thrown away at the boundary.
themes.text: The system already knows most of what the surfaces fail to say. The resource ledger computes bodies, bytes, 725 parse passes and a worst source at 14 of 16 and no renderer reads it (L11-F2, L11-F5); the grammar-failure reason is computed and discarded (S7-F1); external_ref is written on every materialization and never read back (L10-F4, L2-F2); the same-revision path join is exact for 206 of 206 anchors and unused (L10-F5); 934 of 934 narrative anchors resolve while the endpoint hardcodes citable:false (S6-F4); the reading plan's drift to its fallback is silent (S3-F1); a 500's cause is logged nowhere (S10-F1). By VIS-6 all of it is derived and free to render; by VIS-2 each absence is an Unknown rendered as nothing.

themes.title: Currency has no verb and no second limb.
themes.text: A full re-evaluation costs 2.21 s and 145 MB and there is no way to ask for it: the only rebuild seam fires after a write into Butlers, which is why the owner's daemon served a twelve-day-old evaluation (L11-F1). M2 (ruled, dov.2.x) makes the page confess it is old; nothing makes it new. Staleness has two limbs the page names as one: the observed project moved (98 of 271 sources changed, 12 added) and the observatory itself moved 107 Syzygy commits (L4-F1, L4-F2, S10-F2). The fastest-growing block is read from a shared Dolt server on a clock the git revision does not pin, and its population is not monotonic (L11-F7), so 'what changed' cannot be a suffix. Syzygy's own ~120 evidence records have no currency rule at all (L4-F4, S13-F3).

themes.title: The owner's decisions have no surface, and the one action offered is foreclosed.
themes.text: Thirteen gates wait and 0 of 13 appear anywhere (S12-F1); five of them (dov.18, .21, .22, .28, .30) were drafted, independently reviewed and merged in PR #52 eleven minutes before this run's capture, and no surface says so (S12-F2, confirmed by C1). The decision register has no rows for P-67..P-83 (S12-F3) and ~308k words of packets stand between the owner and a ruling. Meanwhile the product's only button offers the write P-71 Q5 foreclosed, and the panel says it is available (L2-F1); the write-guard that would refuse it exists and the materialize path does not call it (L8-F2). No owner sitting shortens the critical path today (L7-F3), because the ready slices are gated by pick order, not by rulings.

themes.title: Repetition is the reading cost, not only the byte cost.
themes.text: The prior run counted the tuple in bytes; this run counts it in words. 718 identical tuples are ~5,026 visible words, about 53% of the 9,403 words readable in flow (C1-F2 correcting L9-F4). The tuple's jargon appears at word 249 and its legend at word 445 (S1-F1), after 718 uses (S2-F1); epistemic apparatus interrupts every ~210 words (S1-F3); 390 links and 283 toggles share two names (S15-F1, S2-F2); the source catalog is a 194-item flat list (S11-F5). All nine cold-open answers arrive by body word 3,206 and the page never says a reader may stop (L9-F1); the page is 1.23x its sources' length with zero synthesis and zero Inferred claims (L9-F3).

themes.title: Generality is asserted, not measured.
themes.text: The product goal is generalizable manifesto generation and every measurement of it is on one repository. A profile that passes M8's census perfectly still fails Syzygy's own principle, success-criterion and craft-policy shapes (L1-F1); the authority set is a singleton (L1-F5); the generator has no front door (REQ-030/031 adopted, unbuilt) and no evaluation runner (L3-F1, L3-F3), accepts 0 of 283 observed source identities [unverified] (L10-F2), and its example fails its own validator (S9-F2). syzygy-mea, the epic that carries the goal, has zero children and two acceptance criteria that cannot be built without a second project (L7-F5).

themes.title: Boundaries are prose where they should be types or edges.
themes.text: One boundary is typed with 30 refusals over 31 fixtures; the rest live in documents (L8-F1); 27 governance check families check documents, not behaviour (L8-F4). Prohibitions reach agents untyped (L5-F2); no observed column names a governing intent, so no intent-to-work edge exists and the join key renders as inert prose (L5-F1, L6-F3); 0 of 1,460 hrefs cross surfaces at claim level (L6-F1). The WIP-one rule for PocModel is one edge where three are needed and the collision is live in bd ready (L7-F1). The credential store trusts whatever it finds at mode 755 (S16-F1, S16-F2).

themes.title: Evidence discipline is a habit, not a mechanism.
themes.text: Mutation tooling has never run in CI (S13-F1); polaris-generation-core has zero mutation evidence (S13-F2, S14-F2) and the rule-6 record is stale (S7-F2); ~120 evidence records have no staleness sweep (S13-F3); the reading plan drifted unnoticed (S3-F1); the owner walkthrough has no run record (S15 gap); the 1z3.28 flake is uncharacterized (S13-F4). Three agents independently proposed the same sha256 drift instrument against three populations (C1-F1 f). The run's own numbers show the same habit: five agents quoted a character count as bytes (C1-F2).

agents.movement_why: Re-measuring the baseline's own numbers on the fresh capture (fresh-polaris.html, 1,504,691 B, served 2026-09-22 08:11) shows the same shape: 364 details/summary elements share 26 distinct accessible names (283 literally 'Source record'), 1,106 links share 686 distinct names (390 literally 'Exact text'), heading levels still skip (h2->h4, h3->h6, h4->h6; h5 unused), and reaching the catalog still takes ~231 Tab presses (baseline said ~228). polaris-copy.ts's 'Source record'/'Exact text' labels remain static literals (grep confirms no interpolation call site), so M13's dov.13.1 ('interpolated labels') is ruled but not yet landed. Nothing regressed and nothing improved on this surface since 2026-09-13.
agents.gap: The shell's keyboard mechanics are sound and the one part of this surface that scales, because polaris-accessibility.ts drives a real browser through real key presses. But three things undercut the functional tier beyond the already-known M13/P-52 gaps: (1) the checker never exercises the page at the population it ships at (144 fixture focusables vs ~1,471 on the real page, >10x gap), so every green CI run is a false signal about the page a reader opens; (2) the checker has no duplicate/non-distinct-name check, so 283 identically-named disclosures and 390 identically-named links -- the page's largest single navigability defect -- are invisible to it; (3) the epistemic legend explaining the ●/? encoding used on every claim from byte ~34,087 of <main> is deferred to <footer> at byte 1,501,161 of a 1,504,691-byte page, so a reader meets thousands of encoded symbols before their explanation, undercutting the encoding's own "legend always matches a live encoding" design intent (POC-REQ-061). The outline's top-level h2 groups are already reader-phrased ('What Butlers is', 'How Butlers is built'), but the depth-nav's own tiers ('Summary/Catalog/Detail/Exact source', 'Sources/Exclusions/Root index/Contradictions/Gaps') name pipeline stages, not reader questions.

agents.label: L1-portability
agents.surface: Polaris portability — what breaks the first time Polaris renders a project that is not Butlers, after M8 lands as ruled
agents.movement_why: `git diff --stat f4589e2 a4a3451` over the six portability-load-bearing files (project-shape-extraction.ts, project-shape-manifest.ts, model.ts, git-observation.ts, polaris-copy.ts, governance-inputs.ts) returns empty output: not one byte moved since the baseline run. Only four commits touched the two POC source trees at all in that window (2593db7, 2ef68f5, 6c9069b, cb0614a) and none of them is a portability change. M8 is ruled and filed as six beads; nothing has landed. The one thing that would move the tier is not another M8 slice: it is measuring, against a real second corpus, what a profile cannot carry — which this lens did, and the answer is that the tier stays weak even with M8 fully applied.
agents.gap: M8 turns every project-specific VALUE into a loaded field. It leaves every project-specific SHAPE a compiled constant. Measured this session by taking Syzygy's own doctrine, rebinding every heading literal to the exact string each parser demands (a simulation of a perfect M8 profile) and changing nothing else: `principle` still fails `malformed-list` — 'no top-level decimal list' — because Syzygy states its seven non-negotiable rules as bold paragraphs, not a numbered list; `success-criterion` over vision.md fails the same way; `craft-policy` fails `malformed-row` — 'no table' — because Syzygy's reading order is a numbered list of links, not a pipe table. Under the no-partial-set rule that takes the whole of vision.md Unknown, including the three project-account sections that did extract. Add the population rules that find nothing (no roster/, no openspec/specs/<dir>/spec.md, no components.md, no rfcs/README.md) and Syzygy's entire first reading, with M8 fully landed, is two extraction classes out of nine: three project-account sections and six success criteria, all from v1.md and architecture.md. The page's 'What Butlers is', 'Scope and principles' and 'Project catalog' groups would all be Unknown or empty. And there is no wire from that pipeline to the generator that is supposed to write the manifesto from it: `PipelineRequest.sources` is typed `unknown`, zero non-test modules import across the two packages, and the only sources ever constructed are three synthetic strings in a demo. The second project does not need a better profile. It needs a declared grammar of shapes, a seam to the drafter, and an honest count of how much of it Polaris can read at all.

findings.title: The profile carries names, not shapes: a perfect M8 profile still cannot read Syzygy's doctrine
findings.detail: M8 slice 5's declared profile fields are 'the root index path, the layer and pillar vocabulary with labels, the per-source extraction bindings, the tree-population rules with a root-independence flag, the precedence row vocabulary, the catalog keys and the project-account keys' (POLARIS-M8-PORTABILITY-FUNNEL.md:942-950). Every one of those is a NAME. The parsers additionally demand a CONTAINER SHAPE that no listed field expresses: `extractPrinciples` requires an ordered decimal list whose items carry a leading bold span (project-shape-extraction.ts:410-417); `extractSuccessCriteria` requires top-level list items (:430-431); `extractCraftPolicies` requires a pipe table with a `File` column holding a Markdown link (:529-538); `extractRosterIdentity` requires a TOML `[butler].name` key (:548-575); the root summary requires the English cardinal prose form `<decimal> staffers ... + <decimal> domain butlers` (:733). [Observed] Method: I copied Syzygy's own vision.md, v1.md and craft-and-care/README.md, replaced ONLY the H2/H3 heading strings with the exact literals each parser demands (`## What Butlers Is`, `## Non-Negotiable Rules`, `## Reading Order`, `## What v1 Ships`, `## Success Criteria`, ...), changed nothing else, and ran the built `extractSource` from packages/three-surface-poc-core/dist/. Results: project-account-section on vision.md -> extracted 3; **principle -> unknown, malformed-list, line 76, 'no top-level decimal list'**; **success-criterion on vision.md -> unknown, malformed-list, line 232, 'no top-level list'**; **craft-policy -> unknown, malformed-row, line 71, 'no table'**; v1.md project-account-section -> extracted 2, success-criterion -> extracted 6. Because any class failing makes the whole source Unknown with no partial item set (:14-17 of the module header), the three account sections that DID extract from vision.md are discarded too. Nine of the nine extraction classes are keyed by a typed closed union with one handwritten parser each in a `switch` (:590-605); a profile can rebind what a class looks for but can neither add a class nor change how a class reads. Separately, eight compiled source-FILENAME gates sit inside the parser bodies (`vision.md` at :369, :407, :426; `architecture.md` at :380; `v1.md` at :386, :426, :440; `README.md` at :478, :528; `components.md` at :504) and none of them appears in slice 5's field list either. Note M15 (dov.15.1) designs partially-extracted and unenumerated-heading flags — that would let vision.md's three account sections survive the principle failure, which is a real improvement, but it makes the shape failure SMALLER, not DECLARABLE: the principle class would still yield zero for a project that numbers its rules any other way.

findings.title: The first reading of Syzygy, with M8 fully landed, is two extraction classes out of nine
findings.detail: Walked the whole pipeline for Syzygy-as-second-project [Observed except where marked]. Population rules (project-shape-manifest.ts:8-14): rule 3 takes `openspec/specs/<one-directory>/spec.md` — `ls openspec/specs/` returns exactly one entry, `README.md`, zero directories, so **baseline-spec yields zero**. Rule 4 takes `roster/<dir>/butler.toml` plus a sibling `MANIFESTO.md` (:498-503) — `ls roster` returns 'No such file or directory', so **roster-identity yields zero and the MANIFESTO source population is empty**; note the rule itself, not just its path constant, is Butlers' organisational shape (a flat directory of named sub-agents each with a TOML manifest and a manifesto) and it is rule 4 of a four-rule closed set the spec fixes. `topology-component` gates on basename `components.md` (project-shape-extraction.ts:504) — Syzygy has no such file, **zero**. `design-contract` gates on a `README.md` carrying an `Index` heading (:478, :66) — Syzygy's RFCs live at `.syzygy/governance/contracts/rfcs/` with no top-level README.md there (per-RFC subdirectory READMEs only), **zero**. `catalog-entry` needs the nine H3 catalog headings (:55-65) — Syzygy declares no capability catalog anywhere, **zero**. `craft-policy` and `principle` fail on shape per L1-F1. That leaves `project-account-section` (2 items from v1.md, 1 from architecture.md) and `success-criterion` (6 from v1.md). **2 of 9 classes, 9 items total.** I also ran the root-index grammar against all three plausible Syzygy root indexes (README.md, .syzygy/governance/doctrine/README.md, AGENTS.md): every one returns summary absent/missing-heading and precedence absent/missing-heading, so **no stated counts and no layer precedence table** — and precedence drives the whole coverage/reconciliation model (project-shape-coverage.ts:95, :265-290). Mapped onto the page's seven h2 groups from the POSTURE section map: polaris-group-overview ('What Butlers is'), polaris-group-boundaries ('Scope and principles') and polaris-group-catalog ('Project catalog') would render Unknown or empty; polaris-group-capability-detail has no capability to detail. [Inferred] This is VIS-2 working — it fails honestly — but 'honestly Unknown' is not a manifesto, and the product goal the pursuit quotes is generalizable manifesto generation.

findings.title: The seam between the extraction pipeline and the generator does not exist — `sources` is typed `unknown` and nothing crosses
findings.detail: `PipelineRequest` declares `readonly sources: unknown` and `readonly readerQuestions: unknown` (pipeline.ts:22-23). [Observed] Scripted sweep: `grep -rnE "project-shape|PocModel|three-surface-poc-core" packages/polaris-generation-core/src/ apps/three-surface-poc/src/polaris-generation/` returns zero lines — not one module in the generator package or its app-side wiring imports anything from the observation core. Denominator: 11 files in packages/polaris-generation-core/src and 6 in apps/three-surface-poc/src/polaris-generation. The only `PipelineRequest` ever constructed is in pipeline-demo.ts:62, whose `sources` is a three-element literal array built in the same function (:33-38) with hand-written text, and whose `readerQuestions` are three hard-coded strings (:63). So the literal-extraction pipeline that knows what a project declares, and the LLM drafter that would write the manifesto, are two packages that have never met. The generation specification already requires the meeting point to be project-independent: REQ-polaris-generation-001 'Admitted project input' (spec.md:12) and its 'Two project identities' scenario (:20-23) require that 'the unchanged generator accepts each with its own project identity, source references and states' and that 'neither project name nor a compiled content hash requires an application-source edit'. No module owns that boundary today. M8 does not name it: the string 'generation' appears in the funnel only for slice 4, which the packet itself calls 'one page, not an implementation' and 'proposes no part of the LLM pipeline and writes no code'.

findings.title: Most of the page's proving-case name is in repair-route sentences that M8's portability census never counted
findings.detail: M8's Gate 1 motif states the copy measurement as '4 of the copy table's 191 rows carry a Butlers-domain proper noun, and the page's h1 is one of them' (funnel line 1843; I re-derived the 191-row denominator this session by counting `id:` keys in POLARIS_COPY). [Observed] That census is over the copy table only. Counting the fresh capture instead: `fresh-polaris.html` (1,501,967 bytes as read) contains the proper noun 'Butlers' **95** times, and **52** of those are inside the exact literal substring `in Butlers, then a new snapshot` — 55% of the page's identity leak, in a form the copy table does not hold. Those sentences are built by template literals in polaris.ts: thirteen rendered sites at :419, :423, :425, :427, :432, :441, :671, :673, :675, :677, :679, :681, :683. They are precisely the repair-route prose M4 (P-71 A, 'reason+route on every Unknown') is about to multiply across every Unknown on the page, so the leak grows with the feature. A fourteenth site, :583, hard-codes a catalog display ordering `['Butlers','Staffers','Dashboard','Connectors']` — presentation curation keyed to the proving case's own catalog keys. M13's 'interpolated labels in the copy oracle' (dov.13.1) would make these sentences CHECKABLE by the oracle; it does not make the project name they interpolate come from a profile.

findings.title: The authority set is a singleton keyed by kind, so P-74 Q3's 'second registry entry' has no selection path
findings.detail: [Observed] `PWB_AUTHORITY_ARTIFACTS` is `Readonly<Record<AuthorityKind, string>>` with exactly one filename per kind — one consent record, one policy, one registry entry at the literal path `.syzygy/governance/declarations/adapter-registry/POLARIS-BUTLERS-PROJECT-SHAPE-OBSERVER-CANDIDATE.json` (governance-inputs.ts:36-39). `PWB_ACT_RECORDS` and `PWB_SUPERSEDED_ACT_RECORDS` are the same shape (:47-55). The registry file itself carries `entries: [...]` of length 1 and its single entry's `subject` is `{observingProject: 'project:syzygy', observedRepository: 'repository:butlers-configured-poc'}`. The authority evaluation validates the registry against `expectations.observingProject` (body-read-authority.ts:662) — the OBSERVING project, which is always Syzygy — and not against the observed repository. [Inferred] So after P-74 Q3's ruled three acts land a second consent record and 'a second adapter-registry entry naming that pair', the loader still resolves exactly one registry file by compiled filename and one entry by position, and nothing selects between two observed projects. M8's slice 5 lists governance-inputs.ts among the files it touches, but every description of that touch is about loading the GRAMMAR from the entry, never about making the authority set keyed by observed project; neither 'per-project', 'AuthorityKind' nor 'second registry entry' selection appears anywhere in the packet's slice designs. This is a small change that becomes a blocker exactly when the owner has paid for the acts.

moves.title: Declare container shapes, not just names: a shape vocabulary in the profile with a fail-closed refusal
moves.what: Extend the M8 `ProjectShapeProfile` so that each extraction class binds a declared CONTAINER SHAPE from a small closed vocabulary — `ordered-list-with-leading-bold`, `unordered-list`, `bold-paragraph-run`, `table-with-named-column`, `toml-table-key`, `heading-section-body` — alongside the heading literal it already binds. Rewrite the nine parsers as (shape reader) x (key rule) rather than nine bespoke functions; keep the closed-grammar strictness exactly as it is, including the `ambiguous-leading-label` and duplicate-key refusals. A class whose declared shape the reader does not implement refuses at PROFILE LOAD with a named reason — never silently, never by falling back to Butlers' shape. The shape vocabulary is itself a registry field under the same act, so adding a shape is an owner act, not a rebuild.
moves.why: This is the measured difference between M8 landing and a second project rendering. With a perfect M8 profile applied to Syzygy's own doctrine, three of the classes still fail — `principle` on 'no top-level decimal list', `success-criterion` on 'no top-level list', `craft-policy` on 'no table' — and under the no-partial-set rule that takes the whole of vision.md Unknown. Every project writes its rules in its own container; only Butlers numbers them. Without this, M8 buys a profile that changes what the parsers LOOK FOR and not what they can READ, and the second project's first reading is two classes out of nine.

Derive Butlers' current profile from the existing parsers and prove it byte-reproduces today's manifest and observation digests at the captured revision — M8 slice 1's equality oracle, reused.
2. Refactor the nine parsers into shape readers plus key rules, with the same equality oracle and no behaviour change. This is the mechanical half and it lands as ordinary engineering.

3. Add the fail-closed refusal: a profile naming an unimplemented shape refuses the load with its reason, with a rule-6 mutant per shape proving the refusal and a no-op mutant proving the digest does not move.

4. Retire the eight compiled source-filename gates (project-shape-extraction.ts:369, :380, :386, :407, :426, :440, :478, :504, :528) into the per-source extraction bindings M8 slice 5 already declares, so the parser body holds no path literal at all.

moves.title: One boundary module that projects an observation into the generator's admitted input
moves.what: A single new module — owned by neither existing package — that takes a completed project-shape observation (its model, its per-class items, its Unknowns with reasons, its source anchors and its digests) and produces the generator's `PipelineRequest.sources` and `readerQuestions` as a TYPED bundle, replacing today's `unknown`. It carries the Unknowns through as first-class entries, not as absences, so the drafter is told what the project did not declare. It runs entirely inside the deterministic plane: it dispatches nothing and needs no provider consent to exist or to be tested.
moves.why: The product goal is generalizable manifesto generation, and today the two halves of it have never been connected: `sources` is typed `unknown`, zero non-test modules import across the packages, and the only request ever built uses three hand-written synthetic strings. The generation specification already demands the boundary be project-independent — 'the unchanged generator accepts each with its own project identity, source references and states' and 'neither project name nor a compiled content hash requires an application-source edit'. Until this module exists, a second project cannot get a first reading no matter how good the profile is, because nothing carries what was extracted to the thing that drafts. Naming the seam also fixes the honest thing: the Unknowns are the most important input to a second-project draft, and an `unknown`-typed field cannot promise to carry them.
slice_plan: 1. Write the bundle type and its JSON schema. Replace `PipelineRequest.sources: unknown` and `readerQuestions: unknown` with it. Oracle: pipeline-demo.ts's three synthetic sources still round-trip to the same canonical digest.

2. Write the projection from the observation model into the bundle, including one entry per Unknown carrying its reason and route. Oracle: over the captured Butlers observation, every admitted item and every Unknown appears exactly once, with an item-count reconciliation against the observation's own denominators.

3. Prove project-independence: run the projection over the second-corpus fixtures L1-M3 produces and confirm the bundle is well-formed with mostly-Unknown content and no application-source edit — the generation spec's 'Two project identities' scenario, satisfied deterministically with no provider call.
4. Fold M8 slice 4's 'one profile schema' page into this module's README so the observer profile and the generator's admitted-input profile converge at a module rather than in two documents.

moves.title: Key the authority set by observed project, so the acts the owner pays for can actually be selected
moves.what: Turn `PWB_AUTHORITY_ARTIFACTS`, `PWB_ACT_RECORDS` and `PWB_SUPERSEDED_ACT_RECORDS` from `Record<AuthorityKind, string>` into a set keyed by observed-repository identity, and make the registry-entry selection resolve by the entry's `subject.observedRepository` rather than by compiled filename and array position. The authority evaluation gains one more refusal: an observation request naming a repository for which no consent, registry entry or policy exists refuses with `no-authority-for-repository` rather than silently evaluating Butlers' authority set. moves.why: P-74 Q3 is ruled A: three acts for a test-only self-observation, one of which is 'a second adapter-registry entry naming that pair'. When those acts land, the code cannot use them. This is the one place where a small structural change decides whether an owner ceremony the owner has already agreed to produces anything. It is also the cheapest of the four moves and the one with the sharpest failure mode if skipped: the acts get signed and then the run does not happen.

It is present in this evaluation's own observed work items (fresh-api-poc.json, workItems.kind=observed, 7,527 items, `bu-5o5tk` among them). Yet `materializedBeadId` is null, both the fresh daemon and the owner's 2026-09-10 daemon render 'Not yet materialized.', `relationship:intent-to-work` renders Unknown, and Trajectory renders no demonstrated-item callout. The cause is a single entry point: `resolveMaterializationEpistemic` (model.ts:325) returns Unknown whenever the local `materialization-record.json` is absent, and that file exists nowhere on this machine [scripted sweep: `find / -name materialization-record.json`, 0 hits; the fresh daemon's state dir holds only the credential, pid and logs]. The one field that could re-derive it from the governed plane - `external_ref` - is dropped at observation: the SQL at work-items.ts:87 selects id, title, status, issue_type, priority, created_at, updated_at and closed_at, and `WorkItemFact` (work-items.ts:15-25) has no such field, even though `findByExternalRef` (materialization.ts:224) already knows how to query it and is called only inside the POST path. VIS-6's named violation is 'any other fact living only inside Syzygy'. Two consequences worth stating plainly for the owner: the POC's escape-property demonstration once worked and was recorded (R-POC-PRODUCT-REVIEW.md:102, 'Reused bu-5o5tk in the configured Butlers...'), and today it is unreproducible; and the one thing the escape property ever produced was a self-test closed 38 seconds later, not an intent that molded anything.

findings.title: Every dependency in the model runs claim -> source; nothing runs source -> claims, which is the direction 'the rest of the project molds itself' is asked in
findings.detail: The reverse index the owner needs is already fully present in the model and never traversed. Computed this session over the fresh machine capture [denominator: 876 claim objects - 426 shape items plus 450 facts - each with its `support[]` array]: the support anchors span 207 distinct files and 642 distinct (file, line) anchors; the median file supports 3 claims; the maximum is 187 (`about/lay-and-land/components.md`), and `about/heart-and-soul/v1.md` supports 164, `about/legends-and-lore/README.md` 71, `about/heart-and-soul/vision.md` 36. So a one-line edit to one Butlers doctrine file would move 164 rendered claims, and the number is derivable today with no new observation. The exact-source page, which is where the owner actually reads the sentence that governs, renders 0 `data-claim-id` elements and exactly 6 hrefs - the skip link, the four nav links, and one `/polaris#polaris-source-...` link back to the source's own row in the source list, not to anything that depends on it. The owner can reach the governing sentence and cannot learn what rests on it, which is precisely the question 'will the rest of the project mold itself' asks.

findings.title: VIS-6(a)'s promotion path has no destination for an observed-only project, so a tuned intent about Butlers has nowhere lawful to land
findings.detail: VIS-6 exception (a) licenses unpromoted owner notes and then says what promotion means: 'promoting a note into governance (an annotation or a dismissal) commits it out to the governed plane, attributed and reasoned'. VIS-6's body defines the governed plane as the thing that 'becomes the authoritative source'. For a note about a Butlers claim, that plane is the Butlers repository. VIS-5 names `openspec/**` as a lawful direct-write root, so doctrine does not forbid it in the abstract - but the one registered adapter declares `"writeSurface": []`, `"authorityType": "version-control"` and `"questions": ["What currently exists?"]`, and the 2026-09-02 act bounds it: 'No write... effect on Butlers or on any other repository. The observer registry entry the owner adopted declares an empty write surface; that remains the bound.' So a promoted note has no destination at all: it cannot stay in Syzygy (VIS-6's violation clause is 'any other fact living only inside Syzygy') and it cannot be committed out. [Inferred: the clauses and the registry state are Observed; the dead end is my reading of them together.] The structural point is that doctrine was written assuming every governed project is writable, and the PWB posture created a class doctrine has no vocabulary for - the observed-only project. Until that is named, every tune instrument this lens could propose stops one step short of landing.

The materialize panel renders that state as a first-class fact - the button is disabled (or replaced by the preview alone) with the refusal sentence and the two acts P-71-Q5 names as the route to re-opening it. The POST handler returns a bounded typed refusal - shaped exactly like the existing `ResponseLimitFailure` - before any `bd` process is spawned, and the machine payload carries the same field so an agent reads the same answer.

Today a single click on the one action the product renders would execute `bd create` against the live Butlers Beads server, which the owner ruled foreclosed on 2026-09-21. This costs almost nothing and it converts the POC from a product that documents authority into one that models it - which is the whole claim of the harness half of the thesis.

moves.title: Name the observed-only project in doctrine, and give a promoted note somewhere lawful to land
moves.what: A doctrine amendment naming a third case under VIS-6: a project Syzygy observes but may not write. For that class, the amendment states where a promoted owner annotation or dismissal becomes authoritative - Syzygy's own `.syzygy/governance/` as the governed plane of the observation record, explicitly not of the project - and states what that record may and may not do (it may carry the owner's intent about a claim and its expiry; it may never be cited as the project's own declared artifact, and Polaris must render it as Syzygy's record, never as Butlers' text).
moves.why: This is the one candidate I found that doctrine would genuinely have to grow to admit. VIS-6(a) says promotion 'commits it out to the governed plane, attributed and reasoned', and VIS-6's body makes that plane 'the authoritative source'. For Butlers there is no such destination: `writeSurface` is empty and the 2026-09-02 act holds it empty. So today every promotion path - an annotation, a dismissal with expiry (M12 slice 3), a tuned sentence - dead-ends, and the only alternative is exactly the state VIS-6's violation clause forbids, a fact living only inside Syzygy. The boundary stretched is VIS-6's assumption that the governed plane of a fact is always the governed project. I would not push this until L2-M2 has produced a standing, read-only proof of the loop - the same reasoning M4 gives for holding its own slice 8: a promotion mechanism is worth much less before anyone has watched one round trip land.
slice_plan: 1. A drafted amendment stating the observed-only class and its promotion destination, with the fresh-reader review VIS-3 requires; agents draft, the owner adopts.
2. Only after adoption: the record shape, its rendering as Syzygy's own record beside the claim, and a counterexample test that such a record can never be cited as project-declared text.

findings.title: All 390 exact-source links share one accessible name, 'Exact text'
evidence: .syzygy/local/pursuit-2026-09-22/capture/fresh-polaris.html — python count of '>Exact text<' = 390 (denominator: every source-route href on the page)
findings.detail: Every '/polaris/source' link is rendered as `Exact text` with no aria-label, title, or visually-hidden text that names which source or requirement it leads to; the only distinguishing attribute (`data-depth-source`) is not exposed to the accessibility tree. A screen-reader user navigating the page's 390-item link list (a standard AT workflow on a link-dense page) hears 'Exact text' 390 times in a row with no way to choose the right one without first locating and reading surrounding text for each. VIS-7 requires every rendered internal link to resolve and its encoding to be legible; an accessible name that collides 390 times is not legible to the AT user even though the href is correct. Fix is local: give each instance a distinct name (e.g. include the capability id or source path already carried in `data-depth-source` / the identity).

findings.title: Verifying a citation costs a full page navigation with no inline preview of the cited span
evidence: apps/three-surface-poc/src/polaris-source.ts:118-121 (renders the whole requirement block, one <pre> per requirement, no highlighted sub-span)
findings.detail: The 'Exact text' link is a bare navigation to a new page; nothing at the citation point shows even a snippet of what will be found there, and the destination page renders the full requirement text with no highlighted span tying it back to the specific claim that cited it (resolution.text is the whole selected requirement, joined and dumped verbatim). A reader checking one claim must leave the reading surface, load a second page, and manually re-read the whole requirement to find the sentence that matters. This is the concrete answer to the pursuit's question 2 ('what would make a citation verifiable in one glance'): a hover/inline preview of the specific quoted span, or a highlighted anchor within the rendered requirement block, neither of which exists today.

agents.label: L4-evidence-currency
agents.surface: Evidence currency — time on the Polaris surface: how old the served evaluation is, whether the page can say so, and whether the project's own retained evidence has a currency rule.
agents.movement_why: No shipped code on this lens changed between the prior run and today, and the gap widened. `packages/cap1-core/src/staleness.ts` still exports `assessCurrency`, `CurrencyBoundDeclaration` and `renderSuperseded` with zero callers outside `packages/cap1-conformance` (sweep over apps/ and packages/, excluding node_modules, dist and .worktrees: the only non-definition hits are in req-042 and req-062 conformance tests). `packages/three-surface-poc-core/src/project-shape-model.ts:167` still hard-codes `FRESH` for every claim; `apps/three-surface-poc/src/polaris-copy.ts:46` still says 'fresh — captured at this evaluation.' All 729 claims on the fresh capture carry `data-epistemic-freshness="fresh"` (729 of 729, denominator = every `data-claim-id`); all 699 on the twelve-day-old capture do too (699 of 699). Meanwhile the measured drift grew: 71 of 271 cited sources changed at three days in the prior run, 98 of 271 at twelve days now. M2 and M12 are ruled and filed but unlanded, so the lens moves when they land, not before.
agents.gap: The ideal is a page that makes its own age felt before it makes any claim, and a project whose own retained evidence obeys the currency rule it imposes on the observed project. Today neither holds. The owner's daemon on 7478 has served the same 2026-09-10 evaluation for twelve days; 98 of the 271 source identities it cites have changed content digest since, twelve sources have been added to the project that it has never seen (three RFCs and nine openspec specs), and every one of its 699 claims still renders `fresh` under a legend that defines fresh as 'captured at this evaluation.' M2 is the ruled answer to most of that and is not re-proposed here. What M2 does not reach, and what keeps this surface weak beyond it, is three things. First, the page is stale in two independent dimensions and names neither: the observed project moved, and the observatory itself moved 107 Syzygy commits, and only the first is M2's probe's subject — a reader told 'out of date' cannot tell whether to restart the daemon or accept that Butlers changed. Second, M2 slice 2's act row rests on a head-ref read that cannot compute the counts it promises to render, so the one ready slice that would close this lens may be resting on an authorization argument narrower than its own design. Third, Syzygy applies doctrine's currency obligation to Butlers' claims and to nothing of its own: the fifteen Polaris funnel evidence records on which the owner's P-68..P-83 rulings rest each pin a baseline commit, 93 commits and 131 files have landed since that baseline, and there is no rule saying when such a record is too old to cite and no script that would tell anyone.

findings.detail: The evaluation identity is a three-part snapshot: the observed Butlers revision, a working-tree metadata digest, and the observer revision — the Syzygy commit the daemon was built from. Those are two different kinds of ageing with two different remedies. Between the owner's daemon and today the observed project moved (98 changed sources) and the observatory moved 107 Syzygy commits (a1215918 -> a4a3451, 2026-09-10 to 2026-09-21), which is why the old capture is 2,087,400 B of pre-lane-A renderer and the fresh one 1,501,967 B. The page renders both coordinates only as one opaque pipe-joined string in the last section, and M2 slice 2's currency probe is specified against the repository head alone. So after M2 lands, a reader told 'N sources have changed' still cannot distinguish 'Butlers moved, this reading is out of date' from 'Syzygy moved, this daemon is running an old observatory and a restart would change the page' — and on the owner's actual daemon the second is the one that fired first and hardest. Nothing states when such a record has aged out, and nothing checks. Rule 7 covers a battery report ('valid only for that commit') and rule 10 covers a review's frozen bytes; neither generalizes to an evidence record, and doctrine's currency clause is written about claim classes on the observed project. Two consequences, both measured this session. (a) The declaration is not even uniform: eleven records key the baseline as `commit`, four (m2, m3, m4, m5) as `syzygy_commit`, one nests it as `commit.baseline` — so no script could read them today without special-casing. moves.why: VIS-1 puts truth first and comprehension second, and 'comprehension is achieved by simplifying presentation, never content' — one opaque pipe-joined string in the last section is simplified content, not simplified presentation. Doctrine trust-and-evidence.md:104 requires staleness to be judged at the current evaluation's as-of instant and visible on the primary surface, not buried in drill-down; it exempts no coordinate of the snapshot. This is not a re-proposal of M2's horizon: it is the limb M2's probe design leaves out, and it is the limb with no act exposure.

moves.title: Vision-extending: let the observed project announce that it moved, instead of the observatory asking
moves.what: A re-observe trigger that fires from the Butlers side: a post-commit or post-merge hook, whose text Syzygy publishes and the owner installs by hand in their own Butlers checkout, that POSTs the operator re-observe route on a configured loopback daemon. Nothing polls, nothing is scheduled, and the daemon gains no timer — the trigger is a consequence of an action the owner already takes. The owner's twelve-day gap closes to the length of one commit.
moves.why: FIT TRACE and the boundary it stretches, stated plainly. P-69 ruled 'no timer or background poller on any arm', and a push trigger is neither: nothing in the daemon wakes up and nothing observes on a schedule. But P-69's design argument for arm (a) is that 'a human-triggered re-evaluation keeps re-observation an operator fact, not a background one', and a hook makes it an automatic fact of the observed project's own workflow — the spirit, not the letter, is what this stretches. It also stretches VIS-5 ('Syzygy writes no implementation code; two namespaces'), because the hook is a script Syzygy authors that executes inside the observed project's namespace, and the observation consent act's exclusion list names 'writes to Butlers' — installing a file under .git/hooks is such a write even when the owner's own hand does it. So: prerequisite doctrine amendment, and the owner should hear the cheaper answer first — restart, or M2's operator route, gets most of this value with none of the argument. Scored honestly low on that basis.

What moved is the specification, not the loop: the understanding amendment was adopted at 3cf5635, adding REQ-polaris-generation-030 (accounted unfamiliar-project discovery) and 031 (consequential owner clarification) as v1-mandatory. That adoption makes the prior gap larger and more binding rather than smaller, because the two stages the product's promise rests on are now required behaviour with no code, no bead and no funnel slice. The one thing that would move the tier is a real model in the loop: M7 slice 3's scripted responder is required by its own evidence record to state that model judgement remains unproven, so every slice that ships without one leaves this lens where it is.
agents.gap: The loop is a superbly bounded middle with no front door, no scoreboard and no exit onto the product's own page. Six stages run (inventory, plan, author, edit, fidelity, repair) and every one of them starts from a source bundle and a set of reader questions that somebody else already assembled and handed in as `unknown` (pipeline.ts:22-23). The two stages that carry the actual promise -- Polaris investigates an unfamiliar repository, and asks the owner the few questions that would change the manifesto -- are adopted v1-mandatory requirements with zero implementation and zero scheduled work. The intermediate the whole thing turns on was quietly weakened: the kit specifies a claim ledger of supporting spans, evidence state, intended meaning and qualification edges, and the implemented inventory carries a statement, a kind and a list of source ids, so fidelity can only ever check that a block cites a document, never that a sentence is entailed by 66 characters of it. Nothing anywhere can say whether an output is good: EVALUATION.md is an excellent unimplemented design whose every judgement above 'the JSON parsed' is assigned to independent evaluators who do not exist, have no artifact to produce and no runner to produce it into, and the only thing binding a prompt version is a SHA-256 equality test that detects that a prompt changed and can never tell whether it improved. And the loop's output has nowhere to land: the generator cites `sourceId` handles over text blobs while the page speaks `data-claim-id` over an evaluation, so the two engines cannot compose even in principle.

findings.title: The loop has no front door: discovery and clarification are adopted, v1-mandatory, and entirely unbuilt and unscheduled
evidence: docs/design/polaris-product-understanding/VISION.md (product promise: 'they do not have to assemble source bundles, write the outline or select every diagram')
findings.detail:
`GenerationStage` is a closed union of six names, and none of them is discovery or clarification (prompts.ts:1). `PipelineRequest` takes `sources: unknown` and `readerQuestions: unknown` (pipeline.ts:22-23) and hands both straight into the first stage (pipeline.ts:259), so the run can never report what it looked at and rejected, what it could not reach, or which project boundary it chose -- it has no such knowledge to report. REQ-polaris-generation-030 (discovery) and 031 (clarification) were adopted into the effective specification at 3cf5635, both `Scope: v1-mandatory`, and the amendment's own tasks.md lists 'Implement 030 discovery' and 'Implement 031 attributed clarification' as unchecked obligations. Scripted sweep: the literals `polaris-generation-030` and `polaris-generation-031` occur in exactly 3 tracked files -- the amendment spec, its SYNTHESIS-MAP.json and docs/evidence/polaris-understanding-adoption-manifest-2026-09-13.json -- and in no funnel packet, no design note and no source file [Observed]. A sweep of all 50 open beads for those ids, 'discovery', 'clarification', 'cold reader', 'evaluation harness' or 'golden' returns 5 hits, none of them about the generator (syzygy-u2a.9's own Discovery section, syzygy-kyt's RFC11-4 golden fixtures, and dov.2.2/dov.20's PWB currency clarification scenario) [Observed].

Stage-by-stage, the world-class loop for this product against what exists (answering question 1):
(1) DECLARE -- what a project must state before generation: repository/snapshot, admitted source classes, project boundary, audience, supported profile, content/usage limits, permitted owner participation. PLANNED only: the profile is M8 (dov.8.2/8.3, one profile schema, profile parameter with constants default); nothing carries boundary or audience today except the demo's literal fields (pipeline-demo.ts:32-38).
(2) DISCOVER -- enumerate candidates, disposition each (selected / excluded / unavailable / unsupported form / deferred by budget) with a reason, expose the profile bounds, offer candidate boundaries rather than merging packages. MISSING: REQ-030, no code, no bead.
(3) UNDERSTAND -- a claim ledger with supporting spans, evidence state, intended meaning, qualification and conflict edges. PARTIAL and regressed: see L3-F2.
(4) ASK -- the smallest prioritized group of consequential questions, each naming the evidence considered and what the answer would change, with supported interpretations, free text, leave-unknown and defer. MISSING: REQ-031, no code, no bead.
(5) ARGUE -- a project-specific section order chosen from the evidence. EXISTS (prompts.ts `plan`), bounded at 1-30 sections, but its denominator is the caller's bundle.
(6) DRAFT and EDIT -- EXISTS (prompts.ts `author`, `edit`), with the `edit` stage constrained by validateStage to return exactly the plan's section set.
(7) VERIFY FIDELITY -- EXISTS as a stage; its independence is M7 slice 2 (known) and its fail-closed behaviour is M6 (known); its *checkability* is blocked by L3-F2.
(8) HUMAN REVIEW AND REPAIR -- `repair` stage EXISTS; the human side does not. The only human artifact is a standalone HTML file written by `pipeline-demo-main --out` with no controls, no accept, no reject, no annotation. A route and a drafted-act exit are M7 slice 4 behind gate .22 (known).
(9) PUBLISH onto the Polaris page -- MISSING entirely; see L3-M4.
(10) REGENERATE on source change -- the demo exercises one changed-source case by mutating a literal (pipeline-demo-main.ts:11) and checking nothing about what moved; dependency-aware invalidation is specified (REQ-009) and unbuilt.
(11) EVALUATE -- MISSING; see L3-F3.

findings.title: The implemented intermediate is a strictly weaker artifact than the kit's claim ledger: no supporting spans, no evidence state, no intended meaning, no qualification edges
evidence: docs/design/polaris-product-understanding/VISION.md ('Desired behavior, observed implementation and ongoing work remain separate')
bd show syzygy-mea acceptance criterion 3 ('Structured claims and edges have exact support')
findings.detail:
The kit defines the Claim ledger as 'Claim ID; statement; supporting spans; evidence state; intended meaning; qualifications; conflicting/unknown inputs' (ARTIFACTS-AND-TOOLS.md:32), and its worked example carries character ranges (`support: [{sourceId:'s1', start:0, end:66}]`), a `meaning` class (`declared-intent`) and a qualification edge (`qualifications: [{claimId:'c3'}]`). What the core implements is `entries: {id, sourceIds, statement, kind}` (provider-draft.ts:20), where `sourceIds` is `refs` -- a unique list of source handles with minItems 1 (provider-draft.ts:17) -- and `kind` is a flat enum that contains 'qualification' and 'conflict' as *labels on entries* with no edge to the claim they qualify or contradict. Every downstream block is the same shape: `paragraph = {id, text, sourceIds}` (provider-draft.ts:19), and diagram nodes and edges likewise.

Three consequences, each of which defeats a stated obligation. (a) Fidelity cannot be mechanical. The reviewer can confirm a block names source s1; it can never confirm that s1's bytes 0-66 entail the sentence. The schema's own header comment concedes it: 'Coverage lists record what the reviewer claims to have checked; they cannot prove entailment or inventory completeness beyond the source denominator' (provider-draft.ts:5-7). syzygy-mea's acceptance criterion 3 requires exactly the opposite. (b) Declared and observed cannot be separated inside generated prose, because no field distinguishes 'the README says this is the purpose' from 'the code does this'. VISION makes that separation the product's central honesty property, and the Polaris page already maintains it on the extraction side. (c) A qualification cannot be kept beside the promise it qualifies, because nothing connects them -- the prompts instruct the model to do it ('Keep limits and tensions beside the promises they qualify', prompts.ts `author`), which is instruction where structure is needed.

This is a regression, not an omission: the richer shape was written down first, in the merged kit, and the implementation that followed dropped it. The kit itself now documents the disconnection in the other direction, recording that `polaris.ts`'s renderers 'do not ingest the proposed draft-bundle format above' (ARTIFACTS-AND-TOOLS.md:59).

findings.title: Nothing in the repository can say whether a generated manifesto is good, and EVALUATION.md's weakest link is that every judgement it defines is assigned to evaluators with no artifact and no runner
evidence: docs/design/polaris-product-understanding/EVALUATION.md (Evidence ladder: '[Observed] The current implementation has evidence at the first two levels')
docs/design/polaris-product-understanding/EVALUATION.md (Separate the judgments table: eight judgements, each requiring 'independent evidence')
findings.detail:
Scripted sweep over the 263 .ts/.js/.json/.md files under packages/, apps/, scripts/ and tools/ for the identifiers an evaluation harness would have to mint -- coldReader, cold-reader, goldenCorpus, golden-corpus, evaluationCase, frozenCase, blindComparison -- returns 43 hits, and on inspection every one is the substring 'judge' inside CAP1's `writeJudgment` / `parityJudgment` / walkthrough-judgment vocabulary. Zero hits for any evaluation-corpus identifier [Observed, denominator 263 files]. There is no `docs/evaluation/`, no case directory, no runner script in package.json's 12 scripts, and no evidence record of a performed evaluation among the 113 files in docs/evidence/ (27 of which are generator records, all of them coverage, offer, validation or funnel records).

The weakest link in EVALUATION.md's design, named precisely: the document separates eight judgements and for seven of them the 'independent evidence' column describes work a human evaluator performs -- frozen source facts, cold-reader answers at each stopping depth, real page traversal with keyboard evidence, recorded owner interventions. That is the right design and it is unfalsifiable as written, because the document specifies no artifact those evaluators produce, no place it lives, no identity binding it to a prompt/schema/renderer version, and no runner that consumes it. So the ladder cannot leave level 2 by any amount of engineering; it can only leave by scheduling people, which nothing schedules. The second weakness follows: the document's own defences against a rigged oracle ('The expected-answer artifact is not supplied to the authoring context', 'a held-out case must not influence project-specific recipe tuning', 'retain that evaluator correction and its reason; do not silently rewrite the oracle') are procedural promises with no mechanism -- there is no frozen case file whose digest could prove the oracle predates the draft.

What is recoverable without a single provider call is larger than the document credits: scope-and-discovery accounting, artifact fidelity as span containment, reference integrity, regeneration invalidation, owner-effort counting and operational-bound behaviour are all decidable from artifacts once L3-F2 is repaired. Only understanding, argument and reader experience genuinely need a human or a model.

findings.title: The loop still requires the owner to prewrite the editorial preparation the specification forbids requiring
evidence: docs/design/polaris-product-understanding/EVALUATION.md (Owner effort judgement, blocking finding: 'Owner must prewrite the inventory, argument or finished prose to obtain success')
findings.detail: REQ-polaris-generation-006 says in terms: 'The bounded workflow SHALL prepare or validate the independent inventory and questions from admitted sources, accounting for those calls in its run budget; it SHALL NOT require the owner to hand-author project-specific editorial preparation before starting' (spec.md:302). Today `readerQuestions` is a caller-supplied field typed `unknown` (pipeline.ts:23) and the only caller hand-writes three of them ('Why does it exist?', 'How do the main pieces connect?', 'What remains a human judgment?', pipeline-demo.ts:66). EVALUATION.md names this exact condition as the blocking finding for the Owner-effort judgement. M7 settled which envelope the questions ride in and explicitly decided them to be prepared acceptance criteria rather than authored argument; it did not make anything prepare them. The consequence is sharper than an unmet clause: reader questions are the loop's acceptance criteria, so a caller who writes easy questions gets a passing manifesto, and the producer's denominator is once again the producer's.

findings.title: Prompt versions are pinned by a hash change-detector, so a prompt edit is detectable but a prompt regression is not
findings.detail: `promptForStage` mints `polaris-<stage>-v1` (prompts.ts:29); the version rides the envelope (pipeline.ts:176) and lands in `StageReceipt.promptVersion` (pipeline.ts:95, 254). Scripted sweep for `promptVersion` and the six literal version strings across packages/, apps/, docs/ and openspec/ returns: the three pipeline sites, the six SHA-256 rows in prompts.test.ts, one demo assertion that two runs agree, one figure in the M7 funnel evidence record, and one unrelated `kit-understand-v1` in the kit example [Observed]. So the entire binding between a prompt version and the world is prompts.test.ts's table of content digests. That test is valuable -- it makes a prompt edit a deliberate act -- and it is the whole of the regression story: it fires on every edit including improvements, and stays silent on a version that quietly stops preserving qualifications. Nothing records what `polaris-fidelity-v1` was observed to catch, so nothing can tell whether v2 still catches it. This is the mechanism EVALUATION.md's 'regression across prompt versions' needs and the reason a case corpus (L3-M3) is worth more than any further prompt work.

moves.title: Discovery as a produced denominator: the run says what it looked at, what it refused and why, before any model call
moves.what: Replace `PipelineRequest.sources: unknown` with a discovery result the pipeline produces rather than receives. Add a `SourcePopulation` port that enumerates candidates from the admitted tree using metadata only (path, size, form, object id -- no body reads), and a `discovery` record that carries, for every candidate: a disposition from a closed set (`selected`, `excluded`, `unavailable`, `unsupported-form`, `deferred-by-budget`) and its reason; the profile bounds actually in force (languages, source forms, repository shapes, scale caps); and, when several project boundaries are present, the candidate boundaries as an explicit unresolved choice rather than a silent merge. The stopping reason is one of REQ-030's five (supported sufficiency, unavailable source, unsupported interpretation, budget exhaustion, unresolved boundary requiring owner selection). Split the work at the honest seam: the enumeration, the dispositions that follow from profile bounds and permissions, the boundary candidates and the scale accounting are all deterministic and ship with no provider at all; only 'which of these candidates bear on the reader's questions' is a model judgement, and it becomes a seventh stage whose *denominator is the deterministic population*, not its own retrieval.
moves.why: This is the difference between a product and a pipeline. The VISION's promise is that the owner does not assemble the bundle; today the bundle is the input. Worse, without a produced population the run has no denominator, so every later honesty claim -- inventory completeness, justified omission, 'material questions sufficiently supported' -- is measured against whatever the caller happened to hand in. VIS-2 says no evidence means Unknown; a run that never enumerated cannot distinguish 'no such source' from 'I was not given it', which is the precise confusion REQ-030 forbids ('it neither reads the denied content nor substitutes lack of retrieval for absence of a capability'). The deterministic half is cheap, needs no egress and no new read authority when run over the tree the process is already in, and it is the prerequisite for every evaluation judgement about scope.

moves.title: Restore the claim ledger the kit specified: supporting spans, evidence state, intended meaning, qualification and conflict edges
moves.what: Change the inventory stage's output from `{id, statement, sourceIds, kind}` to the ledger the merged kit already defines: every claim carries (a) `support: [{sourceId, start, end}]` -- character ranges into the admitted source, not a document handle; (b) `state` from the project's own three-state vocabulary; (c) `meaning` separating declared intent from observed implementation from proposed work; (d) `qualifies: [claimId]` and `conflictsWith: [claimId]` edges, so a limit is structurally attached to the promise it limits; and (e) an explicit `unresolved` arm with a reason for a claim the sources raise and do not settle. Every downstream block (`paragraph`, diagram node, diagram edge, deep-dive) then cites `claimIds` instead of `sourceIds`, so prose is a composition over the ledger and never a second, parallel route to the raw text. Validation gains one mechanical predicate it cannot have today: a cited span must lie within the named source's bounds and its digest must match, which makes 'this citation does not exist' a refusal rather than a review finding.
moves.why: This is the single change that converts fidelity from an opinion into a computation, and it is the precondition for three other moves. syzygy-mea's acceptance criterion 3 requires 'structured claims and edges have exact support'; spans are what 'exact' means. VIS-2's Observed/Inferred/Unknown distinction cannot survive a schema in which a claim and its source are related only by a document handle -- 'Observed' means the statement was read from the named source, and with no offsets nothing can be read back. The kit wrote this down first and the implementation dropped it, so the cost is recovering a design, not inventing one. The qualification edge in particular is the difference between the prompts asking a model to keep limits beside promises and the structure making it impossible to separate them.

moves.title: A frozen-case corpus and an evaluation runner that decides every judgement decidable without a provider, and prints the rest as Unknown
moves.what: Give EVALUATION.md a file format and a runner. Each case is `docs/evaluation/cases/<case-id>/` containing `case.json` (repository and snapshot digest, admitted classes, project boundary, audience, profile, content and usage limits, permitted owner participation, and the expected outcome class: supported whole account / bounded partial account / owner clarification needed / unsupported scope) and `oracle.json` (the frozen material source facts with their spans, the reader questions with evidence-backed acceptable answers, the counterexamples to plausible wrong explanations, the required reading paths, the blocking design criteria) -- the oracle written from sources and committed before any draft exists, so its commit order is the proof that it predates the output. A runner (`npm run poc:generation-evaluate`) consumes a case plus a run's artifacts and returns a matrix of met / unmet / unproven / not-applicable over EVALUATION.md's eight judgements, deciding mechanically: scope and discovery (the produced population against the frozen population, with omissions and their reasons), artifact fidelity (every cited span resolves, lies in bounds and matches its digest; every ledger claim is represented or carries a justified omission), reference integrity, regeneration (a changed source invalidates exactly its dependents), owner effort (a count of interventions, not a grade), and operational behaviour (budgets, admissions, uncertain effects). Understanding, argument and reader experience print as Unknown with the reason 'requires an independent human or model judgement' and a route -- never as pass, never as a score. Every case result is stamped with the full `promptVersion` and `responseSchemaVersion` set, so a prompt edit that moves a case is visible at the moment it is made.
moves.why: The product's whole claim is that a generated account can be trusted, and today nothing in the repository can be wrong about an output's quality, which means nothing can be right about it either. EVALUATION.md's ladder puts the implementation at levels 1-2 and defines levels 3-5 as human work that nothing schedules; this move builds the artifact that human work would produce into and read from, and in doing so harvests the surprisingly large mechanical fraction for free. It also gives the project its missing regression instrument (L3-F5): a case corpus is the only thing that can distinguish a prompt edit from a prompt improvement. And it is the honest answer to VIS-2 at the product level -- an evaluation that cannot judge understanding should say Unknown with a route, exactly as the page does for a claim.

moves.title: Compose the two engines: generated prose is a function over the page's own claims, and a block's state is the weakest claim it cites
moves.what: Make the generator's citation vocabulary the renderer's `data-claim-id` set at one evaluation, instead of a private set of `sourceId` handles over text blobs. A generated block declares `claimIds`; the renderer places it in the section that owns those claims; and the block's rendered epistemic tuple is computed, never asserted -- it is the meet of the tuples of the claims it cites, so a paragraph that leans on one Unknown claim renders Unknown in place, carrying that claim's own reason and resolution route, and a paragraph citing anything Inferred can never render Observed. Prose and extraction then share one page and one legend: the extracted claims stay exactly where they are, and the generated sentence sits above them as the simplification, with its support one disclosure away. The support half of fidelity becomes set containment -- every cited claim id must be in the rendered claim set at the same evaluation id -- which is checkable by script and cannot be talked out of.
moves.why: VIS-1 orders truth first and comprehension second, and says comprehension is achieved by simplifying presentation, never content. That sentence describes this exact composition and the product has no instrument for it: today the page is 1.5 MB of content with no simplification, and the generator writes simplification with no content. This move is also the only composition that does not weaken the page -- because the tuple is computed from the claims, generated prose cannot introduce an unsupported state, which is the failure mode every reviewer fears when 'LLM prose' is proposed for a truth surface. Two consequences worth putting to the owner: it makes the generator's anchors Syzygy's own evaluation-bound evidence identifiers rather than files inside an observed repository, which is a materially easier reading of RFC7-10's closed target classes than the one M7's Q1 has to ask for; and it gives the first-reading Unknowns somewhere to go, because a generated sentence that cites an Unknown claim is the natural place to state the absence in ordinary words.

moves.title: Make the loop real with zero egress: a provider port that refuses any host but the loopback
moves.what: Build a `generate` adapter that speaks the pipeline's existing port to a model served on 127.0.0.1, refusing at construction any route whose host is not the loopback -- not by configuration, by a constructor that cannot be given anything else. Then run the whole loop against it: real inventory failures, real plan choices, real fidelity findings, real repair cycles, real evaluation-case outcomes, with not one byte leaving the machine. Put the one-line reading to the owner rather than assuming it: the implementation authorization act reserves 'real-project reads, provider egress and destination writes'; a loopback call is not egress on the ordinary meaning of the word, and whether it is nonetheless a reserved 'provider' effect is the owner's reading to make, not the implementation's. The port itself has no default route, exactly as `PipelinePorts.generate` has none today, so the code builds and ships under no new authority; only running it needs the reading.
moves.why: Everything this lens wants to know is blocked on the same thing, and it is not permission -- it is that no model has ever been in the loop. M7 slice 3's own evidence record is required to state that real generation, regeneration and reader-quality obligations remain unproven because its responder was scripted, and that sentence will be true of every future slice that ships without a model. A loopback model buys the entire third rung of EVALUATION.md's ladder ('real bounded provider runs establish execution on actual admitted inputs') at a trust cost of approximately zero, and it buys it now rather than after an egress act. It is also the cheapest way to discover the things a scripted responder structurally cannot show: whether the prompts survive a 1.29 MB envelope, whether the fidelity stage finds planted defects, whether repair converges or thrashes, whether a real model can be made to emit spans at all. Stated plainly so it is not oversold: a small local model's output does not prove a frontier model's output, and the evaluation matrix must record which model produced each result -- which is precisely why L3-M3 stamps the matrix with a version set.

moves.title: Prepare the egress case as a signable artifact: a dry run that produces the exact bytes, so the act signs over one run's envelope digests rather than a capability
moves.what: Build the dossier that must exist before the owner is asked anything about egress, produced by a dry run that performs every step except the send. It contains: the exact canonical envelope per stage with its byte count and digest, and the cumulative worst case including the maximum repair cycles; a content screening report classifying what is inside those bytes by governed class (doctrine files, decision records, RFC modules, observed-project sources) with counts and a stated denominator; a withholding proof -- a scripted sweep showing that the nine withheld Butlers sources and every path the screening policy excludes appear in zero envelopes, with the denominator printed; the provider route's declared retention and training terms as a required field of the route record, so an undeclared route cannot be dispatched to; and the accounting policy's worst-case usage against the budget. The act the owner is eventually asked to sign then names those envelope digests -- one run, one corpus, one route -- rather than granting a capability, which is the only shape consistent with this project's act-bound immutable artifacts. Name the trust cost in the dossier itself, in the owner's terms: the first egress is not the observed project's code, it is Syzygy's own governance corpus -- its doctrine, its decisions and its accepted contracts -- which is the more sensitive of the two, and once sent it cannot be unsent.

What is missing is the thing an owner would actually need in front of them to answer, and none of it exists: nobody can currently say what would leave, in what classes, under whose retention terms, or prove that the withheld material stays withheld. M7 measured envelope size, which is one row of this dossier and the easiest one; the screening, the withholding proof and the route's retention terms are the rows that decide the question. Framing the act over digests rather than a capability is what makes the decision reversible in the only sense that matters -- a second run needs a second act -- and it matches how every other consequential change in this project is bound.

moves.title: The attributed owner answer as a first-class, non-derived record that both engines read
moves.what: Give REQ-031's clarification its record and put that record on the surface. A question names what cannot be determined, the evidence considered, and which part of the manifesto the answer would change; it offers supported interpretations, free text, an explicit leave-unknown and a defer. An answer is an `AttributedAnswer`: who said it, when, at which snapshot, with a revision chain and a dependency edge to every artifact that consumed it, so a withdrawal invalidates exactly those and nothing else. The extension beyond the specification is where it lives: the same answer store is read by the extraction engine, because an owner answer is exactly the class of thing literal extraction can never find -- declared purpose, intended beneficiary, which of two documents is authoritative -- and it is the honest filler for a first-reading Unknown whose resolution route says 'ask the owner'. Rendered, it is never Observed and never Inferred: it is attributed, it names its author and its date, and it says in place that it establishes intent and not implementation.
moves.why: VIS-4 says humans steer the vision and agents draft, and the loop currently has no aperture through which a human can steer anything -- there is no question, no answer, no input of any kind between the source bundle and the HTML file. VIS-6 is the clause this stretches: the surface is derived, with exactly two exceptions, the owner's note and personal presentation state. An attributed answer is a third non-derived thing and it is materially different from the note, because prose cites it, extraction consumes it, and its withdrawal invalidates dependents -- a note that nothing depends on is safe in a way this is not. That is the trade the owner should be asked to make deliberately: the surface stops being purely derived, and in exchange the product stops requiring that every true thing about a project already be written down somewhere in it. The alternative is worse and is the current state: an unestablished purpose stays Unknown forever even when the one person who knows it is reading the page.

agents.label: S16-authority-consent-boundary
agents.surface: Authority, consent and the security boundary (body-read authority, credentials, tailnet/browser-origin, machine contract)
agents.movement_why: No prior tier existed for this exact surface grouping. This run assigns a first tier: the authority-evaluation logic (body-read-authority.ts, owner-act-record.ts) is thorough (195 closed invalid cases, real SHA-256 digest binding, doctrine-aligned same-origin checks matching SEC-1 nearly verbatim), but the credential/state-directory boundary SEC-1 depends on has a live, Observed gap -- the running pursuit daemon's own state directory is mode 755, not the 700 the code documents, because ensureCredential() never corrects a pre-existing directory's mode (confirmed live and via a synthetic Node repro).
agents.gap: The three-authority evaluator and its parser are the strongest code here: 195 independently-reachable invalid cases, a recomputed SHA-256 digest checked against the bytes actually read, fail-closed A1 correlation, and browser-origin checks that reproduce SEC-1's doctrine text almost verbatim. But the credential SEC-1 requires for machine clients is minted into a directory whose 0700/0600 invariant is documented but never enforced or verified on reuse: ensureCredential trusts any existing non-empty file at the credential path without checking directory mode or ownership, and Node's mkdirSync({recursive:true,mode}) is a no-op on a pre-existing directory. Combined with a fully deterministic default state-dir path (sha256(repoRoot) under OS tmpdir) on a shared multi-user host, a local actor who pre-creates that path before first run controls its permissions and can plant or swap the trusted token with no check catching it. This run's own daemon demonstrates the gap empirically (755 directory, invariant silently unmet) from benign harness plumbing alone -- nothing in the code would catch a hostile actor either. The credential file itself was 0600 in every case inspected, and no credential bytes were observed leaked.

agents.surface: Polaris as a machine consumer surface: what an agent holding one work item and this daemon can learn, may not do, and may lawfully return
agents.movement_why: Nothing on the agent-facing path changed between the two runs. `GET /api/poc/briefing` on the fresh daemon (127.0.0.1:40003, Syzygy a4a3451) returns 404 `{"served":"nothing","reason":"unknown-route"}`; the literal `mayNot` occurs 0 times in the 5,600,304-byte fresh machine capture; `challenge` is `"unchallenged"` on 1176/1176 claims; `workItems.items` still carries exactly 9 flat fields across 7,527 items. M1 lane A shrank the HUMAN page (2,132,656 -> 1,504,691 B) but the machine payload is untouched: `/api/poc` is still 5.6 MB and `/api/poc/polaris` 654,001 B. M5 (dov.5.1) is filed and ready, not built. The one thing that would move the tier is a join from a work item to the intent that governs it (L5-M1); M5's briefing route, as designed, is keyed `for=<claimId>` and explicitly rejects `for=change:` for now (docs/design/POLARIS-M5-AGENT-BRIEFING-FUNNEL.md:900,995), so it answers about a claim, never about the bead the agent was handed.
agents.gap: Polaris is an excellent read-only encyclopaedia of the observed project and a dead end for the agent doing the work. Handed one bead id and this daemon, an agent spends 5,622,439 bytes over 2 calls to recover 278 bytes of flat bead record and can answer exactly one of its four questions - where is the exact source. The bead id occurs twice in the whole 5.6 MB payload, both times as the same bare row; there is no edge from any work item to a capability, spec, claim or requirement, so 'what intent governs this work' is unanswerable. 'What may I not do' is answerable only about Syzygy's own authority (M5's mayNot), never about the observed project, whose own prohibitions sit as free English inside 18 of 450 facts and whose 194 baseline-spec and 35 design-contract items ship a bare key with no statement at all. 'What is Unknown about my subject' cannot be asked: the 12 Unknown claims are not joinable to any work item, and their 12 resolution routes are English phrases from a hand table that name no act, no artifact and no identifier. And there is no return path of any kind - not a write, not a read-only one: `CHALLENGE_STATES` is a one-member enum, so the closed reason `challenge-suspended` that the act-bound vocabulary already reserves is unreachable and occurs zero times on either surface. An agent that finds Polaris wrong has nowhere to put it.
