moves.title: The challenge channel: the smallest lawful return path, and it writes nothing into Butlers
moves.what: An agent that believes a claim is wrong writes one file into Syzygy's OWN tracked corpus - `.syzygy/governance/challenges/<claimId>.md` - through the ordinary PR flow. It carries the stable `claimId`, the challenger's identity, one counter-citation by `sourceIdentity`, and one sentence. Nothing is POSTed; the daemon stays GET-only and the state dir is untouched. The next evaluation reads that directory (Syzygy's own tree - no new consent, no second repository, no egress), widens `CHALLENGE_STATES` to `['unchallenged','challenged']`, and where the challenge disputes the claim itself sets the already-declared Unknown reason `challenge-suspended` with its already-declared route. A challenge can only REMOVE confidence: it never makes anything Observed, because nothing about Butlers was observed by writing it. The owner resolves by directing a re-observation of the cited source; the claim returns to Observed on the new evidence, never on the agent's word, and the resolution is recorded.
moves.why: This is exactly VIS-4's shape - agents draft, never adopt - and it honours P-71-Q5 in full: the ruling foreclosed the write into Butlers, not the existence of a return path. Every part is already built and dead: claimId is documented as stable across evaluations, every one of the 1,176 claims carries a `challenge` field pinned at one value, and the act-bound closed twelve already reserves `challenge-suspended` with the route 'Challenge resolution'. Without this, an agent that reads a requirement through the exact-source route and finds Polaris misrepresenting it has no lawful way to say so, and Polaris's own honesty depends on nobody ever being right about that.

(a) On every statement-bearing item, add `normative: {force: 'prohibition'|'obligation'|'permission', scope}` derived ONLY from the literal grammar already present in the source (MUST NOT / SHALL NOT / 'must not' / 'must never'), with everything unmatched left explicitly Unknown and counted against the 426-item denominator. moves.title: The frontier and the lane register: one published fact each worker reads alone
moves.what: Two read-only registers on the machine channel and the Trajectory page. (a) Frontier: each non-closed work item carries its blocker set as observed, or an explicit Unknown with a route - today 141 items are rendered 'Blocked' with the blocker silently absent. (b) Lanes: a `lanes` register naming each declared WIP-one lane, its rule quoted from the governance record that declares it, and its current occupant work item or `free`. moves.title: Name the machine reader: per-agent credentials that identify and are forbidden to coordinate
moves.what: Replace the single machine credential with a credential class that carries a stable agent identity. The daemon stays GET-only and serves every agent the same bytes; the identity does exactly two jobs - it names the challenger on a return record (L5-M2) and it names the occupant of a lane (L5-M4). The boundary is held by an explicit stated rule, tested: Polaris never serves one agent any fact about another agent's reads, claims or activity, and never varies a response by reader. A minted identity is refused; identities come from the registry entry, like every other authority.
moves.why: Both lawful agent-facing mechanisms this lens found need a subject, and today every machine reader is the same anonymous bearer of one token. An unattributed challenge is not a draft, it is an anonymous assertion, which is precisely what VIS-4 refuses. This is vision-extending because knowing who is reading is one step from brokering between readers, and 'no unattended agent coordination' is a standing prohibition of the implementation-authorization act. It stretches that clause and must therefore carry its own guard in the same amendment: identity without any reader-visible cross-reader fact.

agents.label: L6-cross-surface
agents.surface: Cross-surface and three-state (Polaris / Trajectory / Orrery / home)
agents.movement_why: Re-measured on the fresh 2026-09-22 captures: 12 of 1,460 hrefs across the four pages leave the page they are on, and all twelve are the same four-item nav bar repeated per page, each marked data-claim-role="non-normative-framing" data-presentation-artifact data-non-citable. Hrefs from a claim to its subject on another surface: 0 of 1,460 (baseline 0 of 1,439; the denominator grew only because Polaris gained 45 source links). The word "desired" still occurs exactly once across all four pages, still from the one hardcoded sentence at apps/three-surface-poc/src/routes.ts:85. Shared element ids: home and Orrery share 21; every other page pair shares exactly one (main-content). Nothing regressed, so the tier does not move down - but the asymmetry widened: lane A left Polaris carrying 729 claims each stamped with the evaluation identity 730 times, while Trajectory and Orrery still name no evaluation at all, so the two surfaces are now further apart in epistemic fidelity than they were at baseline.
agents.gap: Four pages still behave as four products that happen to share a stylesheet. Each is internally link-complete - 0 of 1,054 in-page fragment hrefs fail to resolve - precisely because no link ever leaves its page. Four disjoint address spaces are in use at once (Polaris: data-claim-id / data-anchor-id; home and Orrery: entity:<kind>:<id>; Trajectory: #workitem-bu-*; Orrery's map: district:<path>), and RFC-0006 already names exactly one of these as lawful while naming "work-item row" as an example of a handle that may never be a selection identity. The reader who wants to follow one capability from what it is supposed to be, through what work exists, to where the code lives must carry the identifier in their head across three page loads, re-find it under a different spelling each time, and cannot tell whether the three answers were computed together, because two of the four pages print no evaluation identity. The ideal is not more links: it is one selection reference that every surface resolves identically, pinnable in a URL, with a resolution outcome for the case where a surface has no projection, so that one capability card - owned by Polaris, embedded as the drawer on the other two - carries the desired, execution and observed states side by side under one evaluation stamp.

findings.title: The cross-surface selection mandate is formally written out of scope by the POC's own coverage matrices
findings.detail: RFC6-1 through RFC6-5 - one selection identity space, everything selectable one way, cross-surface synchronization, stamped evaluation defaulting, and the nine typed resolution outcomes - are each rowed `believed-not-applicable` in the PWB contract-coverage matrix, with the [Inferred] rationale "no cross-surface selection-reference interface is introduced". The three-surface change folds RFC6-18's evidence drawer away ("the dedicated evidence drawer container / 'Why this answer?' naming is not built") and omits RFC6's selection/drawer/scenario limb from RFC8-31 entirely ("no drawer/selection UX in the POC-REQ list"). So the surfaces are not failing an unwritten ideal; they are conforming to a written exclusion. What makes this a defect rather than a scoping choice is that the owner's own active generation change - syzygy-mea's `polaris-manifesto-generation` - carries a full NAVIGATION-CONTRACT.md restating the same obligations verbatim ("The same selection is openable across surfaces; lack of a surface projection is handled explicitly rather than losing the selection", "Not-applicable belongs only to a surface... names the surfaces where the selection projects"). The generated product is specified to have cross-surface selection; the thing being generated today is specified not to.

Trajectory's materialize panel prints `Governing intent: REQ-switchboard-identity-001` and `External reference: syzygy-poc:work:whatsapp-single-event-normalization` inside <dd> elements - the second of those is character-for-character the entity id that home and Orrery already use as an HTML id (`work:whatsapp-single-event-normalization`) and that Polaris names in its relationship block. The address exists, the target exists, and the model already holds both ends. This is not a missing computation; it is a rendering that discards a computed edge.

.syzygy/local/pursuit-2026-09-22/capture/fresh-polaris.html: 'REQ-switchboard-identity-001 -> Single-event sender normalization work: Unknown - The human-triggered materialization step has not run.'
findings.detail: The Beads query is `SELECT dolt_hashof('HEAD') AS revision, id, title, status, issue_type, priority, created_at, updated_at, closed_at FROM issues` and WorkItemFact carries exactly those fields. No column that could name a governing intent, spec or capability is read, so no observed intent-to-work edge can exist for any of the 7,527 observed items. The visible consequence: Polaris answers "what work exists for this capability?" with Unknown because the POC's own materialization button has not been pressed, while one page away Trajectory renders a real open Butlers bead, bu-dojk4 "Consolidate WhatsApp identity design after change archival", about that same capability. Both answers are individually honest. Together they are the divergent-truth-by-projection failure RFC-0006 section 2 names as "collectively fatal to the observatory's reason to exist".

findings.title: Two of four human pages carry no evaluation identity, so the reader cannot tell the surfaces were computed together
evidence: .syzygy/local/pursuit-2026-09-22/capture/fresh-trajectory.html: 0 occurrences; footer reads only 'Beads Dolt revision uvgnjtpnr8o0uqmvcgi5s2cje52aiepm.'
findings.detail: RFC6-15 requires every answer to name the evaluation identity it was computed at, and RFC6-3 requires a surface that can only answer at a different evaluation to render the skew explicitly, naming both identities. Home and Polaris print the full composite evaluation identity plus the as-of instant. Trajectory prints a Dolt content hash; Orrery prints a Butlers git sha; neither prints an as-of instant (0 occurrences of 'as of' on either page). To a reader those are three unrelated numbers for what is in fact one evaluation - `model.evaluation` is already on the model these renderers receive. Distinct from M2's Polaris currency work and from M11's operability status line: this is the one string that lets a reader trust a comparison between two surfaces at all.

findings.detail: Answering the lens question about 'one search': there is no filter, no type-ahead and no text input anywhere on the four pages, so the only way to find a claim among 729, a bead among 286 rendered (of 7,527 observed) or a district among the 6,749 files is browser find-in-page, which cannot cross a page boundary. The naive fix - ship a client-side index with the page - is foreclosed: Polaris is already at 72% of its ceiling, and M13's stateless jump list is explicitly the shape chosen instead. RFC6-13 points the other way: anything a surface renders is queryable, so the query belongs on a route keyed by the selection reference, not in the page body. Recorded as a finding rather than a move because the move that would satisfy it is L6-M1's route, not a separate search feature.

moves.title: One selection reference, resolvable on every surface, with a capability card as its drawer
moves.what: Introduce a single selection address - the RFC6-1 tuple (entity kind, durable entity identity), optionally qualified by evaluation identity - carried as a query parameter on all four human routes (`/?select=`, `/polaris?select=`, `/trajectory?select=`, `/orrery?select=`). Every surface resolves the same reference to one of the closed outcomes RFC6-5 names, and every surface that resolves it renders the SAME card body from one shared renderer: what the thing is supposed to be (desired), what work and materialization exist for it (execution), and what is observed about it (observed), each with its own epistemic tuple and provenance. A surface with no projection renders `not-applicable` in place of its own view and still shows the card and names the surfaces where the selection does project - never a dead end. Polaris owns the card: it is the surface whose job is comprehension of one capability, and its existing one-capability-in-depth section becomes the card's canonical rendering; Trajectory and Orrery embed the identical body as a drawer above their board and map.
moves.why: This is the single change that turns four pages into one product. agents.label: L8-boundary-probe
agents.surface: The NOT-boundaries that bind Polaris: what each one is, which instrument holds it, what it costs today, and whether anything but prose enforces it
agents.movement_why: No prior lens examined the prohibitions themselves. The ledger states it: "the prior run's findings were all mandate-grounded; no lens questioned the NOT-boundaries." The prior run's sixteen moves all took the boundary set as given and asked what could be built inside it; this is the first pass over the boundary set as an object of design. [Observed] in LEDGER.md and in docs/pursuits/2026-09-13-vision-pursuit-data.json, where no move's prerequisite is "doctrine amendment".
agents.gap: Syzygy holds itself to a standard nothing else in this repository is held to: every claim typed, every refusal named, every population counted. Its prohibitions are the exception. Exactly one boundary family - the consented body read - is typed as code, with 30 named refusals and a 31-row fixture matrix that mutates each field and asserts the exact refusal. Every other boundary is a sentence: no egress, no second repository, no write into Butlers, no execution of observed code, no unattended coordination, no timer. The registry entry the owner signed declares four of those as typed JSON fields - executeObservedCode false, workingTreeRead false, databaseAccess empty, networkAccess empty - and one file in 112 non-test sources reads them, as a precondition for a read, never by the code path each field names. The project has already built the guard twice: body-read-authority.ts for reads, and cap1-daemon/src/write-guard.ts, a fail-closed, four-refusal, conformance-tested runtime guard for VIS-5's write boundary. The POC daemon imports escapeHtml and createDaemon from that same package and not the guard, and its one write path shells out to `bd create` against another repository with no authority reference anywhere in the file. The second half of the gap is pricing. Most of what reads as doctrine is not: SEC-2 explicitly permits provider egress under named-provider consent, the one-repository and no-write bounds are the 2026-09-02 consent act's scope, the no-timer rule is not a prohibition at all but a recorded absence of authorization, and "no unattended agent coordination" lives in AGENTS.md and in the implementation-authorization act, never in doctrine. Three boundaries are genuinely doctrine - VIS-2, VIS-4, VIS-5 - and those three are the ones that should never move. Because the instrument is nowhere written down beside the boundary, work gets costed at the most expensive ceremony the project has (a doctrine amendment, which needs owner adoption and a fresh-reader review) when a dated act would do, and the owner cannot see which of the bounds around their own product is a principle and which is a paperwork state.

findings.title: One boundary is typed and tested; the rest are prose. The registry's own no-network and no-execute fields are read only as preconditions for a read
findings.detail: [Observed] `evaluateBodyReadAuthority` defines 30 distinct refusal names (scripted count over `name: '<slug>'` in body-read-authority.ts) and its test drives a 31-row fixture matrix that mutates one field per row and asserts the exact refusal. That is the project's own standard for a boundary crossing, and it is applied to exactly one crossing: the consented read. Line 677 is the whole enforcement of four further bounds - `typed['executeObservedCode'] !== false || typed['workingTreeRead'] !== false || !isEmptyArray(typed['databaseAccess']) || !isEmptyArray(typed['networkAccess'])` - and a scripted grep over the TypeScript sources finds one non-test consumer of those four identifiers (body-read-authority.ts itself; the only other hits are that file's test fixtures and one project-shape-observation test asserting the JSON literal). They are read as preconditions of a read. Nothing consults them at the point where network access would happen, and nothing consults them at the point where observed-repository mutation happens. Denominator: 112 non-test, non-declaration .ts sources under packages/ and apps/; 17 import node:child_process; 14 write files; 0 consult an authority evaluation before doing so. The consequence is architectural, not hypothetical: the fields the owner signed are decorative for every effect except the one that was already gated.

findings.title: The runtime write guard for VIS-5 exists, is fail-closed and conformance-tested - and the one daemon that can mutate another repository does not use it
findings.detail: [Observed] `write-guard.ts` is the pattern this lens would otherwise have had to invent: a single sanctioned runtime write path for CAP1-REQ-061, judging the normalized path, resolving symlinks before any write, with a closed refusal set (`degenerate-input`, `traversal`, `symlink-escape`, `outside-governed-plane`), a stated fail-closed polarity - "no check failure ever falls through to a write" - and a conformance test of its own. [Observed] The POC imports `escapeHtml`, `createDaemon`, `Route` and `RouteContext` from `@syzygy/cap1-daemon` in six files and never imports the guard or core's `authorizeWrite` (scripted grep over apps/three-surface-poc/src, packages/three-surface-poc-core/src and packages/polaris-generation-core/src: 0 hits). [Observed] `materialization.ts` contains zero occurrences of `authority`, `consent`, `registry`, `act` or `writeSurface` as a check (grep over the file: the matches are prose in comments and a repository-mismatch string compare); it calls `execFileSync('bd', [...,'create',...])` and `execFileSync('bd', [...,'close',...])` directly, and main.ts mounts `materializeRoutes` unconditionally with `targetRepoRoot: repoRoot`. This is a different claim from the ledger-adjacent one about what the page says: the page's copy can be repaired and this code path would still be, by construction, incapable of refusing. The enforcement artifact is thirty lines away in a package the app already depends on.

findings.title: Most NOT-boundaries are act scope or a recorded absence of authorization, not doctrine - and pricing them as doctrine overcharges every move that touches one
findings.detail: The register, boundary by boundary, with the instrument that actually holds it. [Observed citations; Inferred classification.] (1) NO PROVIDER EGRESS - not a doctrine prohibition. SEC-2 permits it: "Onboarding consent must name the providers permitted for a governed project and the content classes that may be sent." The bar today is two act texts: the generator implementation act's "Real-project reads, provider egress and destination writes remain separately admitted", and the consent act's exclusion list. Instrument: consent record + dated act. (2) ONE REPOSITORY and (3) DECLARED-PROJECT-SHAPE-TEXT ONLY - the 2026-09-02 consent act's scope ("Excluded: ... network egress, writes to Butlers, and any second repository"). Instrument: act. (4) THE RETURN PATH NEVER WRITES INTO BUTLERS - P-71-Q5 states the exact ladder: "a future run needs (1) a dated owner act naming the write, (2) a registry-entry amendment act taking writeSurface from empty to the named path, in that order, then a fresh implementation authorization." VIS-5 names `openspec/**` as a lawful direct-write root, so doctrine is not the bar. Instrument: two acts. (5) NO TIMERS OR POLLERS - not a prohibition at all. The M2 packet's ruled row reads "No act found that authorizes a background poller", and an earlier draft that leaned on AGENTS.md's unattended-coordination sentence was withdrawn by review ("a single daemon's timer is not agent coordination"). Instrument: absence of authorization; curable by one act, with no clause to amend. (6) NO UNATTENDED AGENT COORDINATION - AGENTS.md:99 and the implementation-authorization act and its continuation; nowhere in doctrine. Instrument: act. (7) DAEMON NEVER EXECUTES OBSERVED CODE - SEC-3 is doctrine and self-suspending: "The profile contract is RFC material and blocking: no observed-project code executes until that RFC is accepted." [Observed] `.syzygy/governance/contracts/rfcs/` holds RFC-0001 through RFC-0009 and candidates add RFC-0010 and RFC-0011; no execution-profile RFC exists in either. Instrument: doctrine plus an RFC nobody has drafted. (8) SYZYGY NEVER WRITES IMPLEMENTATION CODE (VIS-5), (9) UNKNOWN IS NEVER GREEN (VIS-2), (10) AGENTS NEVER ADOPT DOCTRINE (VIS-4) - doctrine, and VIS-4 carries its own amendment mechanism. Count: of ten boundaries, three are doctrine clauses, five are act or consent scope, one is a doctrine clause suspended on a missing RFC, and one is not a prohibition. The cost of getting this wrong is paid in the direction that hurts: a move whose real prerequisite is one dated act gets written up as "doctrine amendment", the most expensive ceremony the project has (VIS-4 owner adoption plus a VIS-3 fresh-reader review), and is therefore deferred. Nothing in the repository states the instrument beside the boundary; it is recoverable only by reading six artifacts in the right order.

findings.title: The automated governance battery checks documents, never behaviour: 27 check families, none evaluating a runtime prohibition
findings.detail: [Observed] A scripted sweep over scripts/check_governance.py (7,936 lines) finds 58 CG identifiers resolving to 27 families, CG-1 through CG-27 (CG-77 and CG-99 are invented names used only inside the self-test). Read by their own registered titles, all 27 check artifact hygiene: link and path resolution (CG-1a..1i), retired acceptance phrases (CG-2a..2f), candidate and acceptance banners (CG-4, CG-5, CG-6, CG-27), act digests and wave manifests (CG-7a..7h), context budgets (CG-8, CG-20), duplicate authority homes (CG-9), git-ignore rules (CG-11), dependency edges (CG-13), install routes (CG-14), clause routing (CG-17), fixtures (CG-18, CG-24), substrate pins (CG-19), vocabulary (CG-22, CG-23), battery parity (CG-26). Zero evaluate a runtime effect: not one asks whether a code path can write outside the governed plane, reach a network host, execute observed code, or mutate another repository. The battery that runs on every commit is a document checker. The two places where a boundary IS mechanically enforced are unit and conformance tests in the TypeScript tree, and neither is reachable from the governance battery, so a prohibition's enforcement status is not a fact any Syzygy surface or check can report. Under VIS-2's own rule, a boundary with no enforcement evidence is Unknown, not held - and nothing anywhere renders that Unknown.

findings.title: The one-repository bound inverts the owner's own proving-project ordering, and the envelope that justified the bounded posture already names a provider budget
findings.detail: Question 1 asks for the condition that justified each boundary when it was adopted. For the one-repository bound the record is unambiguous and it points the other way. [Observed] A6, ruled 2026-08-19, states the owner's envelope: "First proving project: The syzygy repository itself; second: butlers", and in the same table "Model/provider budget ceiling: $200/month (Codex monthly subscription)". Thirteen days later the 2026-09-02 consent act bounded observation to Butlers and excluded "any second repository" and "network egress". The bounded posture therefore did not come from a scope statement - the scope statement named two projects and a provider budget - it came from the shape of the ceremony that was affordable to perform first. Today the ordering is inverted: Butlers is the observed project, and observing syzygy itself is the thing that needs three separate acts (P-74 Q3: consent record, second registry entry, secret-policy extension) and is scoped "test-only". [Inferred] The condition that would justify holding the bound - that no second corpus is wanted, and that no provider is paid for - was never the recorded condition; both were stated by the owner before the bound existed. This is the evidence an amendment would rest on, not an argument for making one (VIS-4).

findings.title: The boundaries that should stand, one line each
findings.detail: Question 3, answered as a result rather than padded into moves. VIS-2, Unknown is never green: this is the product; it costs nothing and buying anything with it would end the thesis. VIS-4, agents draft and never adopt: the owner's reading burden is real (other lenses have measured it) but the remedy is cheaper packets, never a delegated adoption. VIS-5, Syzygy never writes implementation code: the north star routes through workers by design and VIS-5 says so explicitly, so the regeneration ideal is not blocked by it - no ready bead is. SEC-3, observed code is never executed: no bead in the backlog wants it, the blocking RFC does not exist, and the cost today is zero. SEC-5, secrets never indexed: the nine withheld Butlers sources are the boundary working. VIS-7's trust floor and trust-and-evidence.md's "inference holds challenge authority only": these are what make the page believable; the only pressure on them is convenience. No unattended agent coordination: act scope rather than doctrine, but the condition that justified it has not changed - nothing in the backlog needs two agents to talk, and the one agent-facing need another lens found is a per-reader identity, which does not require coordination. Six of ten boundaries should stand exactly as written; what they lack is not revision, it is a typed guard and a place where a reader can see that they are held.

moves.title: Reuse the guard the project already built: one typed, fail-closed effect authorization, consulted by every effect path, with a sweep that finds the paths that are not
moves.what: A pure `effectAuthority(registryEntry, effect)` in three-surface-poc-core, written exactly like `evaluateBodyReadAuthority` - same artifact-field reader, same named-refusal return, same fixture-matrix test - but taking an effect descriptor instead of a read: {kind: 'repository-write' | 'process-execution' | 'network-call' | 'body-read', target, detail}. Its refusals come from the registry fields that already exist and are already signed: `write-surface-empty`, `execute-observed-code-forbidden`, `network-access-empty`, `database-access-empty`, `repository-not-observed`. Wire it at the three effect points that exist today: materialization's `defaultRunCreate` and the close path (repository-write, which refuses on `writeSurface: []` before the bd process is spawned), the verbatim route's `git cat-file` (which must AUTHORIZE, proving the gate is not a write-only alarm), and `PipelinePorts.generate`, whose adapter is constructed through the gate so that no provider adapter can exist while `networkAccess` is empty. Then the part that keeps it honest: a sweep test that enumerates every non-test source importing `node:child_process` or writing files (17 and 14 today, denominators printed in the assertion) and requires each to be either behind the gate or on a declared operator-tooling allowlist with a one-line reason. New entries fail the build.
moves.why: The repository's own rule is that a boundary crossing is typed and tested, and the repository has already proved the pattern twice - body-read-authority.ts for the read (30 refusals, 31 fixtures) and cap1-daemon/src/write-guard.ts for VIS-5's write namespace (four refusals, fail-closed, conformance test req-061). Neither is applied to the only daemon in the project that can mutate another repository, and the app already depends on the package that holds the guard. moves.what: A drafted amendment - drafted, never adopted (VIS-4) - that does two things in one artifact. It names a class doctrine has no word for: the self-observed project, the observing project holding a consent record and registry entry over its own tracked governed corpus. And it pays for that permission in the same breath with a rule of the same shape as trust-and-evidence.md's treatment of inference: Syzygy's observations of itself carry no positive status authority - they render as self-observed, they may raise a challenge or a gap, and they never satisfy Syzygy's own trust floor, release gate or any claim that Syzygy is aligned, converged or genome-complete. The evidence the draft would carry is already on disk: A6's owner statement naming "The syzygy repository itself" as the FIRST proving project; P-76 Q2's already-ruled reading that "an observing project reading its own tree ... needs no consent record, registry entry or act" for the generator's own corpus, which is the same act sitting one scope-step away from the observation pipeline; the three-act ladder P-74 Q3 priced for a test-only self-observation; and the [Observed] fact that the three doctrine files contain no mention of the reflexive case at all.
moves.why: The boundary this stretches is not a clause, it is the unstated assumption underneath them: vision.md calls Syzygy "an orthogonal plane: governance artifacts living alongside each governed project", and every rule downstream is written for an observatory that is not its own subject. That assumption is why observing the project the owner named first costs three ceremonies and is scoped test-only, and why the product's proving ground is the project the owner named second. The condition has changed twice on the record: the 2026-09-12 product goal is generalizable generation across projects, and P-76 Q2 has already ruled the reflexive read lawful in the generator's own lane, so doctrine is now silently inconsistent about the same act depending on which pipeline performs it. The no-self-certification half is what makes this safe to even draft: without it, naming the reflexive case would let the observatory's account of itself count as evidence about itself, which is the one failure trust-and-evidence.md is built to prevent. This is a shape, not a recommendation to adopt (VIS-4); its value is that the owner can see the trade in one artifact instead of inferring it from a scope exclusion.

agents.surface: Polaris reading, measured as time-to-comprehension: the cost of getting the owner's sentence ("open one place, understand what a project's vision and goals are") answered from the fresh capture.
agents.movement_why: No prior run measured comprehension cost, so there is no tier to move. What the fresh capture shows against the two prior readings of this territory (S1 "solid" first reading, L2 "world-class" cold-open, owner aborted the walkthrough 2026-09-05 as "Polaris unusable") is that both prior verdicts and the owner's are all defensible at once, because they measured different distances into the same document. The first 639 body words of the fresh capture are a good manifesto (S1/L2 are right); the page as served is 10,173 visible body words and 26,630 with its 364 disclosures opened (the owner is right). Nothing on the page reconciles those two facts for a reader, which is exactly what this lens says is missing.
agents.gap: Polaris is fast to the manifesto and then stops behaving like one. A cold reader reaches the project name in 12 body words, the first project-specific claim in 30, and purpose + promises + deliberate limits complete in 639 words — 2.6 minutes at 250 wpm, zero clicks, sixteen tab stops. Every one of PWB-REQ-021's nine required cold-open answers is reachable inside the first 3,206 body words with two clicks and 88 tab stops. But the page as served is 10,173 visible body words (40.7 minutes) and 26,630 with every disclosure opened (106.5 minutes), and it gives the reader no signal at all that the job ends at word 3,206: the remaining 6,967 visible words (68.5%) are apparatus the nine prompts never need, 4,148 of them a 283-row source inventory rendered in the same linear column, at the same visual weight, as the argument. The surface therefore sets a 40-minute expectation for a 13-minute job. Underneath that, three structural facts: the product's own acceptance criterion for comprehension renders `unknown-never-met` in small muted text at visible word 10,036 of 10,178, 604 tab stops in, and no artifact anywhere in the repo measures what an answer costs — only whether one exists; 718 of the 729 rendered claim tuples are byte-identical, so 28.2% of the visible reading carries two distinct strings; and Polaris contributes almost no words of its own — 526 of the first reading's 645 words (81.6%), and 15,780 of the whole page's 26,635 (59.2%), are Butlers' own literal text, with zero rendered Inferred claims on the entire page. Per equal content Polaris is about 1.23x longer than the text it summarizes. Its real advantage over the README is order and anchors, never compression or synthesis — and it is an advantage only for a reader who knows where to stop.

agents.label: L10-capability-composition
agents.surface: Polaris + Trajectory + Orrery + the generator core, read as a capability set: which pairs compose
agents.movement_why: No prior run tiered composition as its own lens; the closest baseline is prior L6 (cross-surface / three-state, weak), whose finding was that the three surfaces share nothing at claim level. This run refines that: they share nothing RENDERED, but they already share an exact, free join key. [Observed] in the fresh capture, both codeStructure.revision and projectShape.identity.revision are 65af1a0ea2f3c6315a4bec0fe97a2690a18a8694, and 206 of 206 distinct project-shape anchor paths are present in the 6,749-path tree listing (0 missing). Nothing joins them: Orrery renders mappedFileCount 1 of totalFileCount 6749 (fresh-orrery.html data island). Lane A (2ef68f5) and the funnel packets changed page size and doctrine routing, not composition, so no cell moved.
agents.gap: Syzygy holds ten capabilities that are individually careful and almost entirely uncomposed. The composition matrix is nearly empty not because the pieces do not fit but because every consumer is wired to a singleton: Orrery takes two hard-coded declared mappings when the project shape hands it 206 exact same-revision anchor paths; proposed-work is derived for one OpenSpec change when the tree listing holds 59 active ones and the three derivation functions are already general and pure; the materialize action writes an external_ref into Beads as an idempotency key and the work-item observer never selects that column, so the one intent-to-work edge the system has is carried by a file in the daemon's state directory instead of by the governed plane; the generator core's source schema (<=200 entries, a 100-character handle grammar) cannot physically accept the proving case's own 283-source, 131-203-character-identity corpus; and the north-star word, Project Genome, appears five times in all of openspec/, every one a coverage row marked "believed not applicable". The ideal along this lens is that each capability's output is the next capability's input in the governed plane's own vocabulary, so that one edited sentence of intent walks from source to claim to affected authority to dispatched work to observed code region without a human re-deriving the chain. Today that walk breaks at four named steps out of eight. The distance is not doctrinal - eight of the ten pairs with real value are mandate-grounded and need no new authority - it is that nobody has yet made the outputs meet.

findings.title: Project Genome is the north-star capability and no requirement computes any part of it
findings.detail: Scripted sweep over openspec/ with `grep -rniE genome`: 5 hits, denominator 5, and every one is a contract-coverage row whose disposition is 'believed not applicable' / 'Those predicates are not rendered'. Meanwhile architecture.md:143-155 names a six-element universally-required Genome inventory and a five-element required-when-present tier. Mapping those onto the classes the PWB observer actually extracts (scripted over projectShape.classes in fresh-api-poc.json): doctrine -> project-account-section 6 + principle 7 + success-criterion 13; behavioral requirements -> baseline-spec 194; topology -> topology-component 93; quality policy -> craft-policy 7. Two universally-required elements have NO extraction class at all: the verification contract, and the handcrafted/non-regeneratable-region declaration (which architecture.md:145-146 says may be empty but must exist, and whose every listed region is Genome). Of the required-when-present tier only 'accepted load-bearing RFCs' has a class (design-contract 35); explicitly designated executable specifications, generation policy and provenance, normative data contracts and external service contracts have none. So the north-star capability is a doctrine word with no spec, and the two elements that would make a regeneration question answerable are exactly the two that are not modelled. VIS-2 is not violated today only because nothing claims genome-completeness - but nothing renders its absence either, which is the honest thing VIS-2 asks for.

findings.title: The generator core cannot accept the proving case's own corpus: 0 of 283 source identities fit its schema
findings.detail: validateStage builds its source schema as `list(object({ sourceId: handle, text: {maxLength 100000} }), 1)` (provider-draft.ts:109). `list` defaults maxItems to 200 (provider-draft.ts:15) and `handle` is '^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*$' with maxLength 100 (provider-draft.ts:14). Scripted sweep over the fresh capture's projectShape.sources, denominator 283: every identity is of the form `repository:butlers-configured-poc@<40-hex>:<path>#<40-hex>`, lengths 131 to 203 characters, all containing '/' and '#'; 0 of 283 match the handle pattern within 100 characters, and 283 > the 200-entry cap. The generator's source record also carries no revision and no digest (pipeline.ts:22 types `sources` as `unknown`; the schema admits only sourceId and text), so a drafted sentence's citation cannot be the same identity the extracted page cites, and cannot reach the exact-source route. This is the concrete, measured obstacle behind syzygy-mea AC4 ('two real projects through an unchanged generator'): it is reported here as a fact, not re-proposed as a move, because wiring PWB into the generator is mea's and M7's scope. The narrower point that belongs to this lens: the two halves of the Polaris product goal - observe a project's corpus, and draft a manifesto from a project's corpus - speak two different, mutually invalid source vocabularies.

findings.title: The daemon's only re-evaluation trigger is the materialize button for one unrelated WhatsApp work item
findings.detail: `buildModel()` is defined at main.ts:113 and called in exactly two places in the daemon's lifetime: once before `createDaemon` (main.ts:184) and once from `materializeRoutes`'s `onMaterialized` closure (main.ts:200-202). Scripted grep for `buildButlersPocModel|getModel|rebuild|refresh|setInterval|watch` across main.ts, launcher.ts and cli.ts returned 5 hits, all in main.ts, none a timer or watcher. So an owner who edits one sentence of intent in Butlers gets a new evaluation only by restarting the daemon, or by clicking a button that creates a hard-coded WhatsApp sender-normalization bead. This is not an argument for a poller - P-69/RFC2-10 ruled no timer, no poller, and that ruling is right - it is the observation that the human-triggered re-evaluation path already exists and is attached to the wrong verb.

findings.title: The one intent-to-work edge is written into Beads and never read back; the surface claims it from a local file instead
findings.detail: materialization.ts:5-10 states the design intent in its own comment: `externalRef` is 'the idempotency key persisted on the created Bead itself, so a lost local record can still be reconciled without creating a duplicate'. The work-item observer's SQL (work-items.ts:86-88) selects `dolt_hashof('HEAD'), id, title, status, issue_type, priority, created_at, updated_at, closed_at` - nine columns, `external_ref` not among them - and `WorkItemFact` (work-items.ts:15-24) has no field for it. Consequently `model.materializedBeadId` (model.ts:132) and Trajectory's 'demonstrated item' callout (trajectory.ts:150-176) are driven by `materialization-record.json` in the daemon's own state dir (main.ts:114-121), which is Syzygy-local state. model.ts's own comment correctly refuses to treat the record as proof and re-confirms the bead by id against live work items - but it still needs the local file to know WHICH id, so a wiped state dir makes an existing, correctly-referenced bead invisible. The key that would make the edge derivable (VIS-6) is already in the governed plane and unread. The fleet-observability mandate names this exact property as its escape from a terminal cockpit: 'every stream is anchored to the spec and work item that motivated it' (vision.md:229-230).

findings.title: The composition matrix: an exact same-revision path join exists between Polaris's claims and Orrery's map, and nothing uses it
findings.detail: Scripted join over the fresh machine capture: the project shape's 426 items carry 206 distinct anchor paths; the code structure lists 6,749 paths at the same revision; 206 of 206 anchor paths are present in the tree listing, 0 missing. Grouped by Orrery's own district rule (top-level directory, root files as '(root)'): 19 districts, of which 3 contain any anchored path (openspec 194, roster 6, about 6) and 16 contain none - including src (601 files), tests (1,205) and frontend (1,183), 2,989 files with zero declared normative cover rendered. Orrery's declared mappings come from two hard-coded constants (model.ts:235-243 ARTIFACT_PATHS.code/test), which is why mappedFileCount is 1. Matrix cells evaluated in this lens, with the ones that carry real value marked: PWB-extraction x code-map (L10-M1), PWB-extraction x proposed-work x code-map (L10-M2), materialize-action x beads x Trajectory (L10-M3), PWB-extraction x doctrine-inventory (L10-M4), owner-act-ceremony x model-builder (L10-M5), PWB-extraction x readiness-instrument x north-star (L10-M6). Cells evaluated and found empty or already covered: generator x exact-source route (blocked by L10-F2's schema, and the wiring is mea/M7 scope); beads x code-map (no join key exists - bead rows carry no path, and inferring one would violate POC-REQ-052); walkthrough-readiness x generator-fidelity (the generator already validates source references deterministically at provider-draft.ts:90-97, so there is nothing to add); evidence-records x machine-channel (M2's evidence block).

findings.title: One edited sentence of intent: eight steps, three exist, four are missing or closed
findings.detail: The scenario, step by step, with the module that would do it. (1) Owner edits one sentence in about/heart-and-soul/*.md or openspec/specs/<key>/spec.md and commits - Butlers git, outside Syzygy, EXISTS. (2) A new evaluation is minted - MISSING: main.ts:113 rebuilds only at startup and on materialize (L10-M5). (3) The changed source is re-read and its claims re-anchored at the new revision - EXISTS (project-shape-observation/extraction), automatic once (2) runs. (4) The page says what changed between the two evaluations - KNOWN and in flight as M12 dov.12.1, blocked on the retention-posture act .28. (5) The downstream authorities the sentence touches are named - PARTIAL: deriveCurrentAuthority (proposed-work.ts:110-132) does exactly this lookup, for one change out of 59 (L10-M2); the code-side half does not exist (L10-M1). (6) A work item is dispatched - the materialize action exists but its packet is a hard-coded constant (materialization.ts:43-65); a general pure drafter is M4 dov.4.1 (known), and writing a derived item back into Butlers is CLOSED, foreclosed by the 2026-09-02 effect acts, whose registry entry grants read-only authority and an empty write surface. (7) Trajectory shows the resulting bead anchored to the sentence that caused it - MISSING (L10-M3). (8) Orrery shows the code regions the sentence governs - MISSING (L10-M1). Labelled Inferred: the presence or absence of each module is Observed at the cited lines, but the eight-step decomposition is this lens's reading, not a declared contract.
